"""Where was I? One line per project: the first item under `## Next` in docs/STATUS.md.

Sorted by when STATUS.md was last committed, newest first. Flags repos with
uncommitted or unpushed work, since those are the ones a closeout missed.

With --decisions it lists instead every open item under `## Open questions`
(decisions waiting on Eric) across the same repos, then the dated handoffs
written in the window. /startup runs this so a multi-repo day is not reduced
to one repo's "Blocked on" line.

Usage:
    python ~/.claude/scripts/where-was-i.py            # last 14 days
    python ~/.claude/scripts/where-was-i.py --days 60
    python ~/.claude/scripts/where-was-i.py --all
    python ~/.claude/scripts/where-was-i.py --decisions --days 7
"""
import argparse
import glob
import os
import re
import subprocess
from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor
from datetime import datetime, timedelta

DEV = os.path.expanduser("~/Desktop/DEV") if os.name == "nt" else os.path.expanduser("~/DEV")
SKIP = ("_ARCHIVE", "_to_delete", "_OLD_", "worktrees")


def dev_glob(*tail):
    """Glob DEV/*/<tail> and DEV/*/*/<tail>, skipping symlinked top-level folders.

    ~/DEV/_DRIVE links into the Google Drive mount: walking it can hang and
    surfaces local-only projects (DexaProject, Linda_Projects).
    """
    paths = []
    for top in os.scandir(DEV):
        if top.is_dir(follow_symlinks=False):
            paths += glob.glob(os.path.join(top.path, *tail)) + \
                glob.glob(os.path.join(top.path, "*", *tail))
    return paths


def git(repo, *args):
    r = subprocess.run(["git", "-C", repo, *args], capture_output=True, text=True,
                       encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")
    return r.stdout.strip()


def first_next(path):
    text = open(path, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace").read()
    m = re.search(r"^## Next\s*\n(.*?)(?=^## |\Z)", text, re.M | re.S)
    if not m:
        return "(no ## Next section)"
    parts = []
    for line in m.group(1).splitlines():
        s = line.strip()
        if not parts:
            s = re.sub(r"^(\d+[.)]|[-*])\s*", "", s)
            if re.search(r"\w", s) and not s.startswith(("#", "```", "|")):
                parts.append(s)
        elif not s or re.match(r"^(\d+[.)]|[-*])\s", s) or s.startswith("#"):
            break
        else:
            parts.append(s)
    if not parts:
        return "(## Next is empty)"
    item = " ".join(parts)
    return item[:160] + ("…" if len(item) > 160 else "")


CLOSED = re.compile(r"^(~~|answered\b|resolved\b|settled\b|none\b|n/?a\b|nothing\b)", re.I)


def open_questions(path):
    """Open items under `## Open questions`, one string each; closed and blank items dropped."""
    text = open(path, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace").read()
    m = re.search(r"^## Open questions\s*\n(.*?)(?=^## |\Z)", text, re.M | re.S | re.I)
    if not m:
        return []
    items, cur = [], None
    for line in m.group(1).splitlines():
        s = line.strip()
        if re.match(r"^(\d+[.)]|[-*])(\s|$)", s) and not line.startswith((" ", "\t")):
            cur = [re.sub(r"^(\d+[.)]|[-*])\s*", "", s)]
            items.append(cur)
        elif s.startswith(("---", "#")):
            cur = None
        elif s and cur is not None:
            cur.append(s)
    out = []
    for parts in items:
        item = " ".join(p for p in parts if p)
        if not re.search(r"\w", item) or CLOSED.match(item):
            continue
        out.append(item[:220] + ("…" if len(item) > 220 else ""))
    return out

---
name: backup
description: Run the KeystoneOS daily backup on demand (git-push the memory repos, rsync state to Google Drive and the CRASHBOX SSD, reindex memsearch), then report what was saved and what was skipped. Use when the user says "/backup", "run the backup", "back up now", "back my stuff up", "did the backup run", "the backup failed", "I left the laptop off — catch up the backup", or when a session-start HOOK FAILURE names daily-backup. The scheduled launchd job only fires if the Mac is awake at 21:00, so this is the manual catch-up path. NOT FOR whole-stack health checks (use claude-stack-doctor).
---

# Backup

Runs `~/.claude/scripts/daily-backup.ps1` right now. Same script the `com.keystone.dailybackup`
launchd agent runs at 21:00 daily (moved from 09:00 on 2026-09-24, when the Mac became the evening machine) — this is the on-demand path for when the Mac was shut at 21:00.

## Run it

Do not pre-check anything. Run first, report after.

```bash
/usr/bin/caffeinate -i /opt/homebrew/bin/pwsh -NoProfile -File ~/.claude/scripts/daily-backup.ps1 2>&1 | tail -40
```

Use a Bash `timeout` of `600000` (10 min). An awake run takes ~5-10 min, most of it the memsearch
INDEX step. Keep `caffeinate -i`: without it the Mac idle-sleeps on battery the moment the copies
finish, and INDEX crawls through brief dark wakes. On 2026-10-06 that turned a ~6 min index into
2 h. If a run outlasts the timeout, it moves to the background; wait for it, do not re-run.

## Read the verdict from state, not from the tail

```bash
cat ~/.claude/scripts/logs/backup-state.json
```

`status` is `OK` or `ERROR`; `errors` lists the failed job codes. That file is the authority.
The tail is for diagnosing, not for deciding.

**`status: OK` is not "everything was saved" — read `okCount` too.** A run that skipped the
SSD still ends `OK` with 0 errors. See the SSD gotcha below for what the count means.

## Then clear the stale hook error, if any

A failed run appends a line to `~/.claude/global-memory/transcripts/.errors.log`, which is surfaced
as a HOOK FAILURE at every session start. A later successful run does **not** clear it. If `status`
is now `OK` and the file contains only `daily-backup:` lines, archive and empty it:

```bash
cp ~/.claude/global-memory/transcripts/.errors.log ~/.claude/global-memory/transcripts/.errors.log.archived-$(date +%Y-%m-%d)
cp /dev/null ~/.claude/global-memory/transcripts/.errors.log
```

If any non-`daily-backup` line is present, leave the file alone and tell the user what else is in it.
Shell truncation (`: > file`) under `$HOME` is blocked by dcg rule
`core.filesystem:redirect-truncate-root-home`, and there is no `truncate` binary here — use `cp /dev/null`.

## Report

Three lines, plain: did it work, what was skipped, what to do next. Never report "backup complete"
without naming a skipped target — a silent partial backup is the failure this skill exists to prevent.

## Gotchas

**Safe to ignore — expected on a healthy run:**
- `SNAP skip (missing): ~/.codex/memories` — that path has never existed.
- `TARGET baylor deprecated in manifest - snapshots to it SKIPPED` — deliberate.

**Real gaps — always surface these to the user:**
- `TARGET SSD /Volumes/CRASHBOX/AssistantBackup NOT MOUNTED - orphan and working-tree capture SKIPPED`
  — the run still reports `OK` with 0 errors, but **untracked, gitignored, and uncommitted-modified
  files were not saved anywhere.** GitHub and Google Drive cover only committed and pushed work.
  Tell the user to plug in CRASHBOX and run again. This is the most likely way to lose real work.

  **Cross-check with `okCount`, because the error count cannot see this.** `okCount` in
  `backup-state.json` is the number of jobs that ran, and two whole job classes — `CAPTURE`
  (per-project working-tree files) and `STATE-SSD` — exist only when the SSD is mounted. So:
  - **~31 jobs** = SSD captured. **~9-10 jobs** = SSD was absent; only the 4 `REPO` pushes and
    6 Drive `SNAP`s ran (verified against runs on 2026-09-04 and 2026-09-05).
  - A single-digit `okCount` with `status: OK` is the silent partial backup. Say so out loud.
  - Do not derive this from the error count or the exit code — both read `OK` either way.
- `TARGET ... NOT MOUNTED - is Google Drive for Desktop running?` — the Drive app is not running.
  Start it, then re-run.
- `PUSH ERR ... Could not resolve host: github.com` — a network blip, not a repo problem. Confirm
  with `ping -c1 github.com`, then just re-run; the commits are already made locally and will push.
  (Seen 2026-09-04 09:05: both `global-memory` and `skills` failed this way and a re-run fixed both.)
- `repo-diverged:<name>` — automation will never merge. Reconcile that repo by hand. For

# Machine

Machine-specific shell, paths, and traps live in `~/.claude/machine.md`. Read that file first. On a new machine copy `machine.macos.md` or `machine.windows.md` to `machine.md`.

The Mac (`~/DEV`) runs everything. The Baylor Windows laptop (`~/Desktop/DEV`) is used only for desktop-app sessions since 2026-10-21, with no automation. Projects sync through GitHub (`erash11`), documents through Google Drive.

**Session routine.** When working inside a project repo, follow the Session routine in its `AGENTS.md`: `git pull` and read `docs/STATUS.md` at the start; update `STATUS.md`, commit, and `git push` at the end.

# Workflow Expectations

- One home: the "Workflow Expectations" section of `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md`. Read it there.

# graphify

- **graphify** (`~/.claude/skills/graphify/SKILL.md`) — turns any input into a knowledge graph. Trigger: `/graphify`. When the user types `/graphify`, run that skill's workflow before doing anything else.

---

> **Why this file is not identical to `CLAUDE.md`.** Claude Code has a Skill tool, so `CLAUDE.md` routes memory work to the `memory-write` skill instead of restating it. Harnesses reading this file have no such tool, so the memory rules are spelled out below in full. The divergence is deliberate. **Do not symlink these two files together.** The canonical, most detailed copy is `~/.claude/skills/memory-write/SKILL.md` — if a rule below ever disagrees with that file, that file wins.

# Memory System

Two tiers.

## Tier A — per-project structured facts
`~/.claude/projects/<slug>/memory/` — one file per durable fact, indexed by `MEMORY.md`. The active project's Tier A memory is **auto-injected each session**. Write here for stable facts: user profile entries, project conventions, feedback rules. Also indexed by memsearch, so recallable cross-project.

File naming by type: `user_*.md`, `project_*.md`, `feedback_*.md`, `reference_*.md`. Each needs frontmatter (`name`, `description`, `metadata.type`) plus a one-line pointer added to that slug's `MEMORY.md`. `python3 ~/.claude/scripts/remember.py --type <t> --name <slug> --desc "..." --hook "..." [--why ... --how ...] "fact"` does both, refuses duplicates (`--update` replaces), and runs the read-back check; run it from the project folder so the slug is right.

**Slugs.** The slug is the absolute cwd with every character other than a letter or digit replaced by `-`:
- Mac: `~/DEV` → `-Users-kristinarash-DEV` · `~/.claude/skills` → `-Users-kristinarash--claude-skills`
- Windows: `~/Desktop/DEV` → `C--Users-eric-rash-Desktop-DEV` · `~/.claude/skills` → `C--Users-eric-rash--claude-skills`

**Slugs differ per machine.** The same project is `-Users-kristinarash-DEV-<X>` on the Mac and `C--Users-eric-rash-Desktop-DEV-<X>` on Windows. Tier A written on one machine is not auto-injected on the other; memsearch still finds it. Prefer writing durable project facts to the repo's `docs/` so both machines see them.

## Tier B — global working memory
`~/.claude/global-memory/`, loaded every session regardless of cwd:
- `USER.md` — durable user profile. **1,375 character cap.**
- `MEMORY.md` — active threads, environment notes, pending decisions. **2,500 character cap.**
- `transcripts/YYYY-MM-DD.md` — auto-captured turn summaries (Stop hook).

Check `wc -c` before writing. If over cap, consolidate existing entries before adding.

## Daily compiled logs (separate system, read-only)
`~/.claude/claude-memory-compiler/daily/{YYYY-MM-DD}.md`, produced by `claude-memory-compiler` via its own hooks. Only the compiler writes them. Read one only when a question needs that day; the injected snapshot is the source of truth.

## Session startup (read without comment)

> Kept as a manual instruction on purpose. Claude Code does this with the
> `keystone-unified-snapshot.js` SessionStart hook, so `CLAUDE.md` no longer
> states it. Codex has no equivalent hook, so the steps stay spelled out here.
> Do not "align" the two files by deleting this section.
Read in this order: `global-memory/USER.md`, then `global-memory/MEMORY.md`, then `global-memory/transcripts/.errors.log`. The one thing to say out loud: if `.errors.log` is non-empty, give a one-line-per-kind summary (kind, count, latest message) on the first response, then continue. Entries mean a hook or scheduled job failed.

These are a **frozen snapshot** — loaded once. Mid-session writes persist to disk but take effect next session. This preserves the prefix cache. Load anything further only when a question needs it.

## Writing — the steps
On "remember this", "note that", "update memory", "save this", "forget about":
1. Decide tier — "will this be true and useful in 3 months, across projects?" Yes → Tier A. No / only matters now → Tier B.
2. Read the target file in full.
3. Dedup check (substring scan).
4. Cap check (`wc -c`) for Tier B.
5. If over cap, consolidate before adding.
6. Write.
7. Confirm in one line: `Saved — will be active from next session.`

For **remove**: confirm with the user before deleting.

## Retrieval — the tiered ladder
Climb in order; stop as soon as the question is answered. Do not run a search when the answer is already in the injected snapshot.

1. **Tier 0** — scan what is already in context (USER.md, MEMORY.md, today's compiled log). Zero cost.
2. **L1** — `python3 ~/.claude/scripts/recall.py "question"`. Plain code, ~1 s: opens the best file and prints the matching paragraphs. If they miss the answer, open the #2 or #3 candidate it lists.
3. **L2** — on `NO MATCH`, or when the question's words are not the notes' words: `memsearch search "query" --top-k 5`. Hybrid vector + keyword, ~1 min.
4. **L3** — `memsearch expand <chunk_hash>`. Full markdown section around a hit.
5. **L4** — `memsearch transcript <session_id>`. Raw dialogue. Last resort.
6. **Fallback** — "I don't have a record of that."

When Eric corrects a recalled fact, or a recalled answer proves stale, add it to the bench unasked: one `miss` row in `~/.claude/scripts/recall-bench/questions.tsv` (question, file with the right answer, answer), then `CSET=miss bash ~/.claude/scripts/recall-bench/run.sh C`, and say so in one line.

## 1. Read-only

The only writes are the report file and the `Last audited` column of
`~/.claude/rot.md`. **Never delete, archive, disable, or edit a skill during the
audit.** Propose, then wait for approval. A deletion proposal that turns out wrong
is cheap; a deletion is not.

## 2. Step 0 — read `~/.claude/rot.md`

For each layer, compute days since `Last audited`. A layer that is **past due or
`unknown`** is audited this run. A layer inside its window is reported green and
skipped — that is what keeps a monthly run cheap. Read the delegation contract and
the layout invariants in `rot.md` before going further; they bind every step below.

## 3. Step 1 — run the metrics

```bash
python3 ~/DEV/KeystoneOS/scripts/aios-metrics.py
```

Capture every `key=value` line. Any stack trace, or a value like `git_error`,
`no_manifest` or `error_rc…`, is itself a RED finding — do not guess the number.

## 4. Step 2 — assert the layout invariants

| Key | Must be | If not |
|---|---|---|
| `tracked_symlinks_in_canonical` | `0` | RED — a link was committed; Windows gets a dead file |
| `pool_view_drift`, `codex_view_drift` | `0` | RED — someone edited a generated view instead of `~/.claude/skills/` |
| `pool_dangling`, `codex_dangling` | `0` | RED — a deleted canonical skill left an abandoned link |
| `portability_failures` | `0` | RED — see the parity check in Step 4 |

Information, never findings: `third_party_links_in_canonical` (changes with every
install), `pool_third_party`, `codex_third_party` (deliberately preserved installs).

## 5. Step 3 — delegate under the contract

For each due layer, invoke the owner named in `rot.md`, **read-only**:

- Say it plainly in the invocation: *report findings only; apply nothing, write no
  ledger, create no files.*
- `improve-system` applies previously approved proposals in its own Step 0 —
  suppress that explicitly. `brain-audit` appends to its own trend table — suppress
  that too, or leave the Vault layer `unknown`.
- Name the scope you need. Fold the delegate's findings under that layer's heading.
- A receipt covers only what was checked. If the delegate covered less than its
  row claims, write the date **with a scope note**, or leave the row `unknown`.
  Never stamp a date because a delegate exited cleanly.

The Memory (agent) layer has no delegate — audit it directly: every `MEMORY.md`
index line resolves to a file; every memory file appears in its index;
`~/.claude/global-memory/MEMORY.md` is under 2,500 chars; flag time-dimensioned
facts (counters, "still open", past-tense futures).

## 6. Step 4 — the harness layer, audited directly

- **Bloat.** List every canonical skill never invoked in Claude Code transcripts
  (`never_used` from the metrics; name them). Its scope is
  `usage_scope=claude_code_transcripts_only`: Codex and Pi use is not counted.
  If `usage_unreadable_transcripts` is above 0, say so — the list may be too long.
- **Crutch test.** For each never-used and once-used skill, answer the `rot.md`
  question — *would the current model do this fine without it?* Recommend
  DELETE, KEEP (tacit knowledge the model cannot know), or SEASONAL. One line of
  reasoning each. **Never recommend DELETE on `never_used` alone** — it is
  Claude-only evidence. First check Codex:
  `grep -rl "<skill>/SKILL.md" ~/.codex/sessions | wc -l`. A non-zero count means
  the skill may be in use there; report the count. A match can also be a bulk
  scan of the skills folder, so read one hit before calling it real use.
- **Overlap.** Skills whose descriptions claim the same trigger space. Recommend
  a merge, or a sharper `Do not use … (use X)` clause on both.
- **Parity.** Run `python3 ~/DEV/KeystoneOS/scripts/skill-portability-check.py`;
  every failure is a finding. Then check config-level parity, which the linter
  cannot see: list canonical skills set `"off"` in `~/.claude/settings.json`
  `skillOverrides`. Those are hidden in Claude Code but live in Codex and Pi.
  Each one needs a decision: switch it back on, or retire it from canonical.
- **Promotion.** Global skills used in fewer than 2 projects — demotion
  candidates. Project skills used in 2+ projects — promotion candidates.
- **Rules.** Diff `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` against the last 7 days of sessions.
  Report rules contradicted by what actually happened, and corrections the user
  repeated twice that are not yet rules.
- **Hooks.** Compare `hooks_claude` with `hooks_codex`, then diff the two
  directories by name. The copies must match (patch both, always).
- **Agents.** If `agents=0`, report "no agents defined" and skip. Do not invent a finding.

## 7. Step 5 — write the report

Write `~/DEV/KeystoneOS/docs/audits/aios-audit-YYYY-MM-DD.md` with one section per
layer (green-skipped layers get one line). Update `Last audited` in
`~/.claude/rot.md` **only for layers whose check actually ran and produced
output**, then `cp ~/.claude/rot.md ~/DEV/KeystoneOS/docs/rot.md`.

Do **not** write to `docs/audits/aios-trend.md` — `scripts/aios-audit-cron.sh` is
its single writer. If the cron left an uncommitted trend row, commit it together
with this report.

## 8. Step 6 — end with exactly two proposed next builds

Ranked. Each with the one command or sentence that starts it. Not ten. Two.

**Monthly nudge**
```
User: "audit my AI OS"
→ reads rot.md: Skills and Rules past due, Hooks inside its window
→ metrics: all invariants 0; never_used=19
→ delegates nothing for Skills/Rules (owned here); skips Hooks green
→ report with crutch-test verdicts, 2 parity decisions, 2 next builds
```

**One layer**
```
User: "/aios-audit Memory (agent)"
→ audits only the agent-memory stores directly
→ stamps that one row in rot.md; every other row untouched
```

  only. A skill set `"off"` in `skillOverrides` passes it and still never fires in
  Claude Code, while Codex (which ignores that file) loads it. Found 2026-09-12:
  12 canonical skills off in Claude, live in Codex.

  `~/.agents/skills/<owned>/` by path writes canonical. `graphify install
  --platform agents` does exactly that and overwrites the Claude variant — upgrade
  graphify with `--platform claude` only.

  every uncommitted change in the repos it visits. Commit the report as soon as it
  is written, not at the end of a long session.
- **Description length has a budget.** Claude Code caps the combined skill
  description size; very long descriptions risk a skill silently dropping out of
  the listing. When recommending a sharper `Do not use` clause, keep the whole
  description near 650 characters.

  `git` inside command substitution). Use Python `subprocess` or literal paths;
  do not try to bypass the guard.

metadata:

# AIOS Audit — is the harness itself still true?

Five audit skills already exist, and each owns one layer. This skill owns the
layer none of them touch: **the harness** — skill roster, agents, hooks, rules,
agent memory, and parity between Claude Code, Codex, and Pi. For every other
layer it **delegates**; it never re-implements another audit.

| Delegate | Owns |
|---|---|
| `os-audit` (project) | project data: routing, index truth, freshness, duplication |
| `brain-audit` | SecondBrain as a system — the four C's |
| `improve-system` | note-level rot: stale seeds, duplicates, conflicts |
| `claude-stack-doctor` | automation plumbing: launchd, venvs, memsearch, backup freshness |
| `doctor-plus` | context-engineering posture of the workspace |

If `$ARGUMENTS` names one layer from `rot.md`, audit only that layer.

## 1. Read-only

The only writes are the report file and the `Last audited` column of
`~/DEV/KeystoneOS/docs/rot.md`. **Never delete, archive, disable, or edit a skill during the
audit.** Propose, then wait for approval. A deletion proposal that turns out wrong
is cheap; a deletion is not.

## 2. Step 0 — read `~/DEV/KeystoneOS/docs/rot.md`

For each layer, compute days since `Last audited`. A layer that is **past due or
`unknown`** is audited this run. A layer inside its window is reported green and
skipped — that is what keeps a monthly run cheap. Read the delegation contract and
the layout invariants in `rot.md` before going further; they bind every step below.

## 3. Step 1 — run the metrics

```bash
python3 ~/DEV/KeystoneOS/scripts/aios-metrics.py
```

Capture every `key=value` line. Any stack trace, or a value like `git_error`,
`no_manifest` or `error_rc…`, is itself a RED finding — do not guess the number.

## 4. Step 2 — assert the layout invariants

| Key | Must be | If not |
|---|---|---|
| `tracked_symlinks_in_canonical` | `0` | RED — a link was committed; Windows gets a dead file |
| `pool_view_drift`, `codex_view_drift` | `0` | RED — someone edited a generated view instead of `~/.claude/skills/` |
| `pool_dangling`, `codex_dangling` | `0` | RED — a deleted canonical skill left an abandoned link |
| `portability_failures` | `0` | RED — see the parity check in Step 4 |

Information, never findings: `third_party_links_in_canonical` (changes with every
install), `pool_third_party`, `codex_third_party` (deliberately preserved installs).

## 5. Step 3 — delegate under the contract

For each due layer, invoke the owner named in `rot.md`, **read-only**:

- Say it plainly in the invocation: *report findings only; apply nothing, write no
  ledger, create no files.*
- `improve-system` applies previously approved proposals in its own Step 0 —
  suppress that explicitly. `brain-audit` appends to its own trend table — suppress
  that too, or leave the Vault layer `unknown`.
- Name the scope you need. Fold the delegate's findings under that layer's heading.
- A receipt covers only what was checked. If the delegate covered less than its
  row claims, write the date **with a scope note**, or leave the row `unknown`.
  Never stamp a date because a delegate exited cleanly.

The Memory (agent) layer has no delegate — audit it directly: every `MEMORY.md`
index line resolves to a file; every memory file appears in its index;
`~/.claude/global-memory/MEMORY.md` is under 2,500 chars; flag time-dimensioned
facts (counters, "still open", past-tense futures).

## 6. Step 4 — the harness layer, audited directly

- **Bloat.** List every canonical skill never invoked in Claude Code transcripts
  (`never_used` from the metrics; name them). Its scope is
  `usage_scope=claude_code_transcripts_only`: Codex and Pi use is not counted.
  If `usage_unreadable_transcripts` is above 0, say so — the list may be too long.
- **Crutch test.** For each never-used and once-used skill, answer the `rot.md`
  question — *would the current model do this fine without it?* Recommend
  DELETE, KEEP (tacit knowledge the model cannot know), or SEASONAL. One line of
  reasoning each. **Never recommend DELETE on `never_used` alone** — it is
  Claude-only evidence. First check Codex:
  `grep -rl "<skill>/SKILL.md" ~/.codex/sessions | wc -l`. A non-zero count means
  the skill may be in use there; report the count. A match can also be a bulk
  scan of the skills folder, so read one hit before calling it real use.
- **Overlap.** Skills whose descriptions claim the same trigger space. Recommend
  a merge, or a sharper `Do not use … (use X)` clause on both.
- **Parity.** Run `python3 ~/DEV/KeystoneOS/scripts/skill-portability-check.py`;
  every failure is a finding. Then check config-level parity, which the linter
  cannot see: list canonical skills set `"off"` in `~/.claude/settings.json`
  `skillOverrides`. Those are hidden in Claude Code but live in Codex and Pi.
  Each one needs a decision: switch it back on, or retire it from canonical.
- **Promotion.** Global skills used in fewer than 2 projects — demotion
  candidates. Project skills used in 2+ projects — promotion candidates.
- **Rules.** Diff `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` against the last 7 days of sessions.
  Report rules contradicted by what actually happened, and corrections the user
  repeated twice that are not yet rules.
- **Hooks.** Compare `hooks_claude` with `hooks_codex`, then diff the two
  directories by name. The copies must match (patch both, always).
- **Agents.** If `agents=0`, report "no agents defined" and skip. Do not invent a finding.

## 7. Step 5 — write the report

Write `~/DEV/KeystoneOS/docs/audits/aios-audit-YYYY-MM-DD.md` with one section per
layer (green-skipped layers get one line). Update `Last audited` in
`~/DEV/KeystoneOS/docs/rot.md` (the one copy) **only for layers whose check actually ran and produced
output**.

Do **not** write to `docs/audits/aios-trend.md` — `scripts/aios-audit-cron.sh` is
its single writer. If the cron left an uncommitted trend row, commit it together
with this report.

## 8. Step 6 — end with exactly two proposed next builds

Ranked. Each with the one command or sentence that starts it. Not ten. Two.

## Examples

**Monthly nudge**
```
User: "audit my AI OS"
→ reads rot.md: Skills and Rules past due, Hooks inside its window
→ metrics: all invariants 0; never_used=19
→ delegates nothing for Skills/Rules (owned here); skips Hooks green
→ report with crutch-test verdicts, 2 parity decisions, 2 next builds
```

**One layer**
```
User: "/aios-audit Memory (agent)"
→ audits only the agent-memory stores directly
→ stamps that one row in rot.md; every other row untouched
```

## Gotchas

- **Linter green is not parity.** `skill-portability-check.py` reads frontmatter
  only. A skill set `"off"` in `skillOverrides` passes it and still never fires in
  Claude Code, while Codex (which ignores that file) loads it. Found 2026-09-12:
  12 canonical skills off in Claude, live in Codex.
- **Views are links into canonical.** Anything that writes into
  `~/.agents/skills/<owned>/` by path writes canonical. `graphify install
  --platform agents` does exactly that and overwrites the Claude variant — upgrade
  graphify with `--platform claude` only.
- **Concurrent sessions commit your work.** `closeout` in another session sweeps
  every uncommitted change in the repos it visits. Commit the report as soon as it
  is written, not at the end of a long session.
- **Description length has a budget.** Claude Code caps the combined skill
  description size; very long descriptions risk a skill silently dropping out of
  the listing. When recommending a sharper `Do not use` clause, keep the whole
  description near 650 characters.
- **`dcg` blocks some shell shapes** (`rm -rf` inside heredocs, `$VAR` redirects,
  `git` inside command substitution). Use Python `subprocess` or literal paths;
  do not try to bypass the guard.

# rot.md — how fast each AIOS layer goes stale

Audit each layer on its own clock, not all at once. `aios-audit` reads this
file: any layer past due, or marked `unknown`, is a finding.

**A date here is a receipt, not an intention.** Write one only after that
layer's check in the last column has actually run and produced output.

| Layer | Where it lives | Rots | Audit every | Last audited | Owner | Concrete check |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Identity | `global-memory/USER.md` | very slow | 3 months | 2026-09-13 (partial: 7 days of sessions + memsearch, not 90 days) | memory-write | Read USER.md; flag any role, family, or career fact contradicted by the last 90 days of sessions. |
| Substrate | `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `~/DEV/*.md` routers | slow | 3 months | 2026-09-13 (router paths only; project CLAUDE.md internals not checked) | os-audit | Delegate to `os-audit` Check 1 (routing integrity). |

| Agents | `~/.claude/agents/` | fast | 1 month | 2026-09-13 | aios-audit | Count `*.md`. Currently **0 exist** — report "no agents defined" and skip until one does. |

| Memory (agent) | `~/.claude/projects/*/memory/`, `global-memory/` | medium | 1 month | 2026-09-13 (time-dimensioned scan: DEV slug + global only) | **aios-audit itself** | Audited directly — see the delegation contract below. `improve-system` does NOT cover these stores. Check: every `MEMORY.md` index line resolves to a file; every memory file appears in its index; `global-memory/MEMORY.md` is under its 2,500-char cap; flag time-dimensioned facts (counters, "still open", past-tense futures). |
| Memory (vault notes) | `~/SecondBrain/` notes | medium | 1 month | 2026-09-13 (Notes, Knowledge, Projects; 577 notes) | improve-system | Delegate — but read-only, per the contract below. |

## The question that governs a skill's fate

Not "how often did I run it?" but **"would the current model do this fine
without the skill?"** If yes, the skill is a crutch that now limits the model.
Delete it. Keep only skills carrying tacit knowledge the model cannot know:
force-plate thresholds, GPS conventions, Baylor reporting norms, Eric's own
routines.

Seasonal skills (`forecast-capture`, `ingest-book`) are exempt from low-use
pressure. Judge them in season.

## Delegation contract (R2-09)

A delegate is invoked **read-only**, for a **named scope**, and its receipt is
written **only** for the scope it actually covered.

1. **Read-only.** Before invoking a delegate, instruct it explicitly: report
   findings, apply nothing, write no ledger, create no files. Several delegates
   (`improve-system` among them) begin by applying previously approved proposals
   — that must be suppressed. `aios-audit` writes only its own report and the
   `Last audited` column.
2. **Scope must be verified, not assumed.** A delegate's actual coverage is what
   its body scans, not what this table wishes it scanned. `improve-system` scans
   `~/SecondBrain/` — Notes, Knowledge, Projects. It does **not** touch
   `~/.claude/projects/*/memory/` or `global-memory/`. Those are audited by
   `aios-audit` directly.
3. **A receipt covers only what was checked.** If a delegate returns findings for
   a narrower scope than its row claims, write the date **and** a scope note, or
   leave the row `unknown`. Never stamp a date because a delegate exited cleanly.

## Layout invariants the audit must assert

- `~/.claude/skills/` is canonical, is a git repo, and contains **no TRACKED symlinks**
  (`git ls-files -s` shows no mode 120000). On-disk links to third-party skills are
  expected; they are listed in the per-machine `.git/info/exclude` (never the tracked
  `.gitignore`), and a pre-commit hook refuses to commit one. What must never happen is
  committing a link, because Windows pulls this repo and a Mac link is dead there.
- `~/.agents/skills/` and `~/.codex/skills/` are **generated views**. Each carries
  a `.generated-by-sync-to-codex` manifest. Every entry **in the manifest** must be
  a symlink on Mac (a copy on Windows); wrong representation is drift.
- Entries **not** in the manifest are third-party installs (`npx skills add`).
  They are counted and reported, **never** flagged as errors and never pruned.
- Support directories (`_shared/`) have no SKILL.md and must never be pruned.

## Direction of travel

**Fewer skills, stricter rules.** Skills get deleted; rules get sharpened.

## Cadence

Monthly metrics: launchd `com.keystone.aiosaudit`, day 1 at 14:00.
It writes a trend row and a nudge. It does not commit and does not push.
The agentic audit is run by hand: "audit my AI OS" in `~/DEV/KeystoneOS`.

## The question that governs a skill's fate

Not "how often did I run it?" but **"would the current model do this fine
without the skill?"** If yes, the skill is a crutch that now limits the model.
Delete it. Keep only skills carrying tacit knowledge the model cannot know:
force-plate thresholds, GPS conventions, Baylor reporting norms, Eric's own
routines.

Seasonal skills (`forecast-capture`, `ingest-book`) are exempt from low-use
pressure. Judge them in season.

## Delegation contract (R2-09)

A delegate is invoked **read-only**, for a **named scope**, and its receipt is
written **only** for the scope it actually covered.

1. **Read-only.** Before invoking a delegate, instruct it explicitly: report
   findings, apply nothing, write no ledger, create no files. Several delegates
   (`improve-system` among them) begin by applying previously approved proposals
   — that must be suppressed. `aios-audit` writes only its own report and the
   `Last audited` column.
2. **Scope must be verified, not assumed.** A delegate's actual coverage is what
   its body scans, not what this table wishes it scanned. `improve-system` scans
   `~/SecondBrain/` — Notes, Knowledge, Projects. It does **not** touch
   `~/.claude/projects/*/memory/` or `global-memory/`. Those are audited by
   `aios-audit` directly.

   a narrower scope than its row claims, write the date **and** a scope note, or
   leave the row `unknown`. Never stamp a date because a delegate exited cleanly.

# PLATFORM — area index

The agent operating system itself: control plane, tooling, dashboards,
and the CLIs that connect Claude to real apps.

## Control plane

| Folder | What it is |
|---|---|
| `KeystoneOS/` | Map and control plane. Holds `AGENTS.md`, `data/`, `decisions/`, `audits/`, `memory/`, `knowledge/` → own `CLAUDE.md`. **Maps projects by reference — never stores their source.** |
| `project-triage/` | The registry (`portfolio.json`) and the live project board (`pm` / `/pm` → `board.py`): resume cards, focus view, slate cap, 7-day rule, Friday sweep, crosswalk drift, landed ledger. Static `dashboard.html` retired 2026-10-03. |
| `token-dashboard/` | **Deleted 2026-10-03** (Eric). Third-party course clone (`nateherkai/token-dashboard`), never ours. |
| `agy/` | Agency sync helper (`com.keystone.agysync` launchd job) |
| `claude-global-memory/` | Symlink to `~/.claude/global-memory`, the one clone of `erash11/claude-global-memory`. Edit there. |
| `~/.claude/skills/` | Canonical skills repo. Clone of `erash11/claude-skills`, not in DEV. |
| `_ARCHIVE/morning-briefing/` | Retired 2026-08-14, parked 2026-10-23. Do not use. |

## Tooling and experiments

| Folder | What it is |
|---|---|
| `CLI_Dev/` | CLI development scratch. Built CLIs land in `~/go/bin/`. Holds `printing-press/` — the Printing Press workspace (`library/`, `manuscripts/`), moved here from `~/printing-press` on 2026-09-07. Now covered by the backup manifest — but `CLI_Dev` routes to **`ssd` only**, so it is protected only on nights CRASHBOX is attached, not by GitHub or Drive. `~/printing-press` is now a symlink to it; tools that assume the old path still work. |
| `Terminal_Fluency/` | CLI-learning mission. Lessons + quiz. Learns through real repairs, not exercises. |
| `Cloudroom_Learning/` | Cloudroom teaching mission (`/mattpocock-skills:teach`). `MISSION.md`, `reference/` cheatsheet, `lessons/` HTML, `learning-records/`. Own repo, local only. Started 2026-10-14. |
| `Tech_Inventory_Analysis/` | Tech stack inventory |
| `Bucket/` | Catch-all + `docs/TOOLING-OPTIMIZATION.md` |
| `TypeSafe_Sandbox/` | Sandbox for the TypeSafe System One API (the Jev model: typed judgments and probabilities, not generated text). Holds `setup_global_key.sh` and `smoke_test.py`. **The API key is not in the repo, and nothing about it syncs between machines** — Windows reads `~/.claude/typesafe.env` (auto-ignored by the dotclaude whitelist), macOS uses the Keychain (service `typesafe-api-key`) exported by `~/.zshenv`, per the `machine.macos.md` rule. The key starts with `apikey_`; dropping that prefix returns 401. Claude Code carries the matching skill as plugin `typesafe@typesafe-ai`. Per-machine key status: `TypeSafe_Sandbox/docs/STATUS.md`. |
| `agent-skills/` | Agent skills. Repo `erash11/agent-skills`. |
| `Build_Along/` | Build-along project. Repo `erash11/Build_Along`. Purpose to confirm. |

## Routing

- `docs/model-routing.md` — which Claude model to use for each task type (one default per type).

## Generated artifacts (not source)

- `graphify-out/` — workspace knowledge graph. **Stale: last built 2026-04-09.**
  Rebuilding forces a full pass because of the old Windows-era manifest.
- `printing-press-library` — generated CLI library, on GitHub only (`erash11/printing-press-library`);
  local clone removed 2026-10-24 (pp-* skills install from upstream). Not source.

## Connectors already built

In `~/go/bin/`, all made with `cli-printing-press`. Two of them
(`zotero-research-library`, `catapult-openfield-connect`) build from the local
workspace at `CLI_Dev/printing-press/`, not from the public registry:

```
cli-printing-press   espn-pp-cli      fireflies-pp-cli
flight-goat-pp-cli   movie-goat-pp-cli   recipe-goat-pp-cli
zotero-research-library-pp-cli  zotero-research-library-pp-mcp
```

## Scheduled jobs

Seven launchd agents, all local-only — they do not run with the Mac off:
`morning, rituals, reconcile, adjudicate, agysync, dailybackup, stackdoctor`.
`com.keystone.morningbriefing.plist` is on disk but not loaded — a leftover
from the briefing retired 2026-08-14; safe to delete.

## Notes

- Layout rules and the gitignored-subtree trap: `project_dev-layout-and-discovery.md`.
- Agent sessions commit to these repos while you read them. Re-verify git
  numbers at the moment you act, not from an earlier scan.
- Check stack health with `/claude-stack-doctor`.

## Archived 2026-10-03

Read-only on GitHub. Local copies sit in `~/DEV_archive_hold/2026-10-03/` until ~2026-11-02. Records: `project-triage/portfolio.json`.

`CommandCentre` → Project_Triage; `Life-OS` → Project_Triage; `AgentAssist` → Project_Triage; `AI_Analyst`; `PythonScripts_2024`; `KnowledgeManagement` → Flint.

# PLATFORM — area index

The agent operating system itself: control plane, tooling, dashboards,
and the CLIs that connect Claude to real apps.

## Control plane

| Folder | What it is |
|---|---|
| `KeystoneOS/` | Map and control plane. Holds `AGENTS.md`, `data/`, `decisions/`, `audits/`, `memory/`, `knowledge/` → own `CLAUDE.md`. **Maps projects by reference — never stores their source.** |
| `project-triage/` | The registry (`portfolio.json`) and the live project board (`pm` / `/pm` → `board.py`): resume cards, focus view, slate cap, 7-day rule, Friday sweep, crosswalk drift, landed ledger. Static `dashboard.html` retired 2026-10-03. |
| `token-dashboard/` | **Deleted 2026-10-03** (Eric). Third-party course clone (`nateherkai/token-dashboard`), never ours. |
| `agy/` | Agency sync helper (`com.keystone.agysync` launchd job) |
| `claude-global-memory/` | Symlink to `~/.claude/global-memory`, the one clone of `erash11/claude-global-memory`. Edit there. |
| `~/.claude/skills/` | Canonical skills repo. Clone of `erash11/claude-skills`, not in DEV. |
| `_ARCHIVE/morning-briefing/` | Retired 2026-08-14, parked 2026-10-23. Do not use. |

## Tooling and experiments

| Folder | What it is |
|---|---|
| `CLI_Dev/` | CLI development scratch. Built CLIs land in `~/go/bin/`. Holds `printing-press/` — the Printing Press workspace (`library/`, `manuscripts/`), moved here from `~/printing-press` on 2026-09-07. Now covered by the backup manifest — but `CLI_Dev` routes to **`ssd` only**, so it is protected only on nights CRASHBOX is attached, not by GitHub or Drive. `~/printing-press` is now a symlink to it; tools that assume the old path still work. |
| `Terminal_Fluency/` | CLI-learning mission. Lessons + quiz. Learns through real repairs, not exercises. |
| `Cloudroom_Learning/` | Cloudroom teaching mission (`/mattpocock-skills:teach`). `MISSION.md`, `reference/` cheatsheet, `lessons/` HTML, `learning-records/`. Own repo, local only. Started 2026-10-14. |
| `Tech_Inventory_Analysis/` | Tech stack inventory |
| `Bucket/` | Catch-all + `docs/TOOLING-OPTIMIZATION.md` |
| `TypeSafe_Sandbox/` | Sandbox for the TypeSafe System One API (the Jev model: typed judgments and probabilities, not generated text). Holds `setup_global_key.sh` and `smoke_test.py`. **The API key is not in the repo, and nothing about it syncs between machines** — Windows reads `~/.claude/typesafe.env` (auto-ignored by the dotclaude whitelist), macOS uses the Keychain (service `typesafe-api-key`) exported by `~/.zshenv`, per the `machine.macos.md` rule. The key starts with `apikey_`; dropping that prefix returns 401. Claude Code carries the matching skill as plugin `typesafe@typesafe-ai`. Per-machine key status: `TypeSafe_Sandbox/docs/STATUS.md`. |
| `agent-skills/` | Agent skills. Repo `erash11/agent-skills`. |
| `Build_Along/` | Build-along project. Repo `erash11/Build_Along`. Purpose to confirm. |

## Routing

- `docs/model-routing.md` — which Claude model to use for each task type (one default per type).

## Generated artifacts (not source)

- `graphify-out/` — workspace knowledge graph. **Stale: last built 2026-04-09.**
  Rebuilding forces a full pass because of the old Windows-era manifest.
- `printing-press-library` — generated CLI library, on GitHub only (`erash11/printing-press-library`);
  local clone removed 2026-10-24 (pp-* skills install from upstream). Not source.

## Connectors already built

In `~/go/bin/`, all made with `cli-printing-press`. Two of them
(`zotero-research-library`, `catapult-openfield-connect`) build from the local
workspace at `CLI_Dev/printing-press/`, not from the public registry:

```
cli-printing-press   espn-pp-cli      fireflies-pp-cli
flight-goat-pp-cli   movie-goat-pp-cli   recipe-goat-pp-cli
zotero-research-library-pp-cli  zotero-research-library-pp-mcp
```

## Scheduled jobs

Seven launchd agents, all local-only — they do not run with the Mac off:
`morning, rituals, reconcile, adjudicate, agysync, dailybackup, stackdoctor`.
`com.keystone.morningbriefing.plist` is on disk but not loaded — a leftover
from the briefing retired 2026-08-14; safe to delete.

## Notes

- Layout rules and the gitignored-subtree trap: `project_dev-layout-and-discovery.md`.
- Agent sessions commit to these repos while you read them. Re-verify git
  numbers at the moment you act, not from an earlier scan.
- Check stack health with `/claude-stack-doctor`.

## Archived 2026-10-03

Read-only on GitHub. Local copies sit in `~/DEV_archive_hold/2026-10-03/` until ~2026-11-02. Records: `project-triage/portfolio.json`.

`CommandCentre` → Project_Triage; `Life-OS` → Project_Triage; `AgentAssist` → Project_Triage; `AI_Analyst`; `PythonScripts_2024`; `KnowledgeManagement` → Flint.

- `docs/model-routing.md` — which Claude model to use for each task type (one default per type).

- `graphify-out/` — workspace knowledge graph. **Stale: last built 2026-04-09.**
  Rebuilding forces a full pass because of the old Windows-era manifest.
- `printing-press-library` — generated CLI library, on GitHub only (`erash11/printing-press-library`);
  local clone removed 2026-10-24 (pp-* skills install from upstream). Not source.

```

Seven launchd agents, all local-only — they do not run with the Mac off:
`morning, rituals, reconcile, adjudicate, agysync, dailybackup, stackdoctor`.
`com.keystone.morningbriefing.plist` is on disk but not loaded — a leftover
from the briefing retired 2026-08-14; safe to delete.

- Layout rules and the gitignored-subtree trap: `project_dev-layout-and-discovery.md`.

# STORAGE — where every file lives

Read this before you save, move, back up, or copy any file. One rule set for every agent
(Claude Code, Codex, Gemini) on every machine. Decided by Eric 2026-10-16.

## The model

Every file has one **true copy**. Edit the true copy, or a working copy that syncs back to it
the same day. Everything else is a **backup** (machine-written, never edited) or **scratch**
(thrown away).

Drive is the one place Eric looks. Documents live there directly. Code lives in GitHub and is
mirrored into Drive, so Drive still shows everything.

## Where things go

| What you are saving | True copy | Work on it at | Gets back to the true copy by |
|---|---|---|---|
| Document, PDF, deck, spreadsheet for humans | Drive `00_Primary_Storage_Drive/`, filed by its `README.md` ladder | Drive desktop app, or `~/DEV/_DRIVE` | Drive sync (automatic) |
| Finished deliverable from a repo | Drive `00_Primary_Storage_Drive/03_REPORTS/`, named `YYYY-MM-DD_<Sport>_<Topic>_<Audience>.<ext>` | made in `<repo>/outputs/` | `closeout` copies it (copy, keep the repo one) |
| Code, scripts, project docs, `STATUS.md` | GitHub `erash11/<repo>` | `~/DEV/<repo>` | `git commit` + `git push`, every session |
| Generated output (charts, exports, logs) | `<repo>/outputs/` | same | regenerate from code; gitignore it if large |
| Database (DuckDB, SQLite) | local disk, inside its repo or `~/DEV` | same | daily (daytime: hourly 12:00-17:00 via `scripts/daily-backup-login.sh`) `daily-backup.ps1` stages the live DBs (not dated `before`/`backup` copies) into `dev-databases.tgz`, uploaded via `gws` to Drive `_MACHINE/Backups/Machine` (since 2026-10-20; one copy, no history) |
| Secrets (`.env`, tokens, keys) | macOS Keychain or local `.env` | same | nowhere else — never in git, Drive, or chat |
| Claude/Codex config, skills, memory | GitHub `dotclaude`, `claude-skills`, `claude-global-memory` | `~/.claude` | `git push` (daily-backup also pushes) |
| A loose file with no home yet | `~/DEV/_INBOX/` | same | `weekly-review` drains it within 7 days |
| Temporary agent work | the session scratchpad | same | thrown away |

Identifiable athlete health data (`DexaProject`, case reviews like `SpecialRequests/TOS_ES`) stays
where it is: local or its one Drive folder. Never push it to GitHub, never paste it into chat or an
external service. A folder with a `CLAUDE.md` saying "local only" is in this class.

## Machine-written copies (backups)

Scripts write to Drive `_MACHINE/`. Humans browse `00_Primary_Storage_Drive/`. Nothing lives in both.

- `_MACHINE/Cloud_Copy/DEV` — one-way mirror of `~/DEV`, minus databases, secrets, and regenerable/catalog
  caches (`printing-press-library`, `graphify-out/cache`, `.build`, `node_modules`, `.venv`, `__pycache__`).
  Written by `~/.claude/scripts/cloud-push.py` (07:00 and 17:30).
- `_MACHINE/Backups/Machine` — daily (daytime: hourly 12:00-17:00 via `scripts/daily-backup-login.sh`) `.tgz` snapshots of `~/.claude/projects`, Codex, Gemini, and LaunchAgents
  uploaded directly by `gws` API (`daily-backup.ps1` `Snapshot-Gws`); `zotero.tgz` (`~/Zotero` database, PDFs,
  styles) at most weekly and only when Zotero changed (`Snapshot-Zotero`, since 2026-10-23); plus SSD captures of repo data git does not
  carry from `~/.claude/scripts/backup-manifest.json`.
- External SSD `CRASHBOX` — second daily copy when CRASHBOX is plugged in at midday.

Read a backup to restore. Edit only the true copy. To add a path to the backups, add it to
`backup-manifest.json`; a path missing from the manifest is not backed up.

## How agents reach Drive

- Read, list, move, and upload through the API: the `gws` CLI (`gws drive files …`), or the Drive MCP.
  Moves keep file IDs; use `gws drive files update` with `addParents`/`removeParents`.
- The mount (`~/Library/CloudStorage/GoogleDrive-…`) is for Eric and for `cloud-push.py`. Agent
  reads through it can hang, and its view can lag the server by days. Before trusting the mount,
  compare its folder list with `gws drive files list`.
- `gws --upload` only takes a path inside the current directory: `cd` to the file's folder first.

## Places that are never a destination

Baylor OneDrive, `~/Desktop`, `~/Downloads`, and the Drive root. If something lands in one of
these, file it by the table above in the same session.

## Before you finish a session

- Every repo you touched: committed and pushed.
- Every deliverable you made: copied to `03_REPORTS/`.
- Every new top-level folder in `~/DEV`: has a `portfolio.json` row (`new-project` does this).

## Known gaps (2026-10-16)

- The Mac's Drive mount went stale because DriveFS was choked on 68,000+ small files in
  `_MACHINE/Cloud_Copy/DEV` (`printing-press-library`, `graphify-out/cache`, leftover `node_modules`).
  Those folders were trashed on Drive via `gws` and excluded in `cloud-push.py` (cutting the file count
  from 104,945 to ~33,735), and `daily-backup.ps1` now uploads its Drive `.tgz` snapshots, receipt, and
  `RESTORE.md` directly via the `gws` API to `_MACHINE/Backups/Machine`, so a lagging local mount can
  never block nightly backups.
- Night backups failed whenever the Mac slept on battery (every 21:00 run 10-13 to 10-22). Since 2026-10-22 the
  backup runs in the daytime: launchd tries hourly 12:00-17:00 through `scripts/daily-backup-login.sh`, which runs
  it only on AC power, at most 2 tries a day, and stops once a run ends OK.
- `cloud-push.py` could not run straight from launchd (macOS blocks it from Terminal-made Drive files). Since
  2026-10-23 launchd opens it in Terminal via `scripts/cloud-push-launch.sh`; a run that never starts logs an ERROR.
- Windows laptop: retired as a work box 2026-10-14; desktop-app sessions only since 2026-10-21. It follows this same table:
  documents through Drive sync, code through `git pull`/`git push`, never a second true copy.

Background and history: `~/DEV/docs/FILE-ORGANIZATION-PLAN.md`.

The **entire hook directory is mirrored** across two harnesses — not one stray file.
Verified 2026-09-09: ~55 near-identical entries in each of

- `~/.claude/hooks/` — Claude Code
- `~/.codex/hooks/` — Codex

**Patch both, always.** Editing one leaves the other on the old code. Whichever
harness runs next re-triggers the bug, which reads as "the fix reverted".

The two are not exact mirrors, so do not assume drift means a failed patch:
`.claude/hooks/` additionally holds `herdr-agent-state.sh` and an older
`memsearch-sync.js.bak-20260814`. Those are legitimate, not drift.

Worked example — `transcript-capture.js` (Stop hook):
Codex invokes it with a null `transcript_path`, which the script did not handle.
Patched 2026-09-07 to exit quietly on null instead of erroring.
**Tell that a copy drifted:** `missing transcript_path` lines reappear in
`~/.claude/global-memory/transcripts/.errors.log`. When they do, diff the two
copies before debugging the script itself.

Verify after any hook edit — one file, or the whole set:

```bash
diff ~/.claude/hooks/transcript-capture.js ~/.codex/hooks/transcript-capture.js
diff -rq ~/.claude/hooks ~/.codex/hooks     # whole set; expect only the two known extras
```

Hook *failures* surface at session start via `.errors.log` — see
[[keystoneos-verification-habits]] for what a clean exit code does and does not
prove, and [[backup-sync-system]] for the archive-before-clearing rule on that log.

---
name: memory-write
description: >-
  Writes, updates, removes, and recalls facts in the two-tier memory system
  (~/.claude/global-memory/ and ~/.claude/projects/<slug>/memory/). Use for write
  requests such as "remember this", "note that", "update memory", "save this", and
  "forget about", and for recall requests such as "did we already…?", "what did we
  decide about X?", and "do you remember…?". Picks the tier, dedups, and enforces caps;
  recall checks the injected snapshot, then recall.py, then memsearch. Do not use for a story or lesson
  worth a vault note (use capture-insight) or an article to keep (use ingest-resource).
---

# Memory Write

## Outcome
- Fact added to, updated in, or removed from the correct memory tier
- Tier-B caps enforced (2,500 chars for MEMORY.md, 1,375 for USER.md)
- Confirmation: "Saved — will be active from next session."

## Pick the tier first

Ask: "Will this fact still be true and useful in 3 months, across multiple projects?"

**Tier A — `~/.claude/projects/<slug>/memory/`** (one file per fact, indexed by MEMORY.md)
- Durable user facts → `user_*.md` (metadata.type: user)
- Stable project conventions / gotchas → `project_*.md` (metadata.type: project)
- Behavioral feedback rules → `feedback_*.md` (metadata.type: feedback)
- External-system pointers → `reference_*.md` (metadata.type: reference)

**Tier B — `~/.claude/global-memory/`** (single capped file)
- Active threads (in-progress work) → `MEMORY.md` `## Active Threads`
- Current env notes (URLs, tool versions, project structure in play) → `MEMORY.md` `## Environment Notes`
- Pending decisions → `MEMORY.md` `## Pending Decisions`
- Durable user profile updates → `USER.md`

## Steps

1. **Decide tier** using the rule above.
2. **Read** the target file in full.
3. **Dedup check** — substring scan; if the fact already exists, skip or update in place.
4. **Cap check** for Tier B — `wc -c < ~/.claude/global-memory/MEMORY.md` (or USER.md). If over cap, consolidate (merge similar entries, prune stale) before adding.
5. **Write** the change.
   - Tier A: create a new file with proper frontmatter (name, description, metadata.type) and add a one-line pointer to that slug's `MEMORY.md` index. `name:` follows the rule below. Do it in one call, from the project folder (the slug comes from the current folder; `--dir` overrides):
     `python3 ~/.claude/scripts/remember.py --type <t> --name <bare-slug> --desc "<one line>" --hook "<when to open>" [--why "..." --how "..."] "<fact>"`
     It checks the name rule, refuses an existing or look-alike name (exit 2: read that file, then `--update` it or `--force`), writes the file and the index line, runs steps 1 and 4 of the Verification Gate, and refreshes recall.py's index. `PASS` covers those checks; step 3 (contradictions) is still yours.
   - Tier B: append under the correct `##` section.
6. **Confirm** in one line: `Saved — will be active from next session.`

## The `name:` field — bare kebab slug

**`name:` = the filename stem minus its leading type token, kebab-cased.** The type
already lives in `metadata.type` and the filename already carries the prefix; repeating
it in `name:` is the third copy.

| File | `name:` |
|---|---|
| `project_automation-cadence.md` | `automation-cadence` |
| `user_sports-teams.md` | `sports-teams` |
| `reference_baylor-house-style.md` | `baylor-house-style` |
| `feedback_project_idea_capture.md` | `project-idea-capture` |

Note the last row: strip only the **leading** token. `feedback_project_idea_capture.md`
is a feedback memory *about* project-idea capture — its name keeps the word `project`.

`[[links]]` target this bare name, never the filename and never a prefixed variant.

This rule exists because it was previously unwritten: an audit on 2026-09-02 found the
corpus split 59 bare / 58 prefixed, which broke 37 links. Both forms look right in
isolation, so without a stated rule the split regrows on every write.

## Actions

- **add** — append (default)
- **replace** — substring match + swap. Preferred over add when updating an existing fact.
- **remove** — confirm with the user before deleting.

## Retrieval — the tiered ladder

When the user asks about past context, decisions, or "did we already…?", climb in order and stop as soon as the question is answered. Do not run a search when the answer is already in the injected snapshot.

1. **Tier 0** — scan what is already in context (USER.md, MEMORY.md, today's compiled log). Zero cost.
2. **L1** — `python3 ~/.claude/scripts/recall.py "question"`. Plain code, ~1 s: BM25 keyword rank over the memsearch paths plus the whole vault, a Tier A memory first, then it opens the best file and prints the matching paragraphs with line numbers. Answer from that. If the printed paragraphs miss the answer, open the #2 or #3 candidate it lists.
3. **L2** — on `NO MATCH`, or when the words in the question are not the words in the notes: `memsearch search "query" --top-k 5`. Hybrid vector + keyword, ~1 min: Tier A files (including the Windows-machine slugs), daily logs, transcripts.
4. **L3** — `memsearch expand <chunk_hash>`. Full markdown section around a hit.
5. **L4** — `memsearch transcript <session_id>`. Raw dialogue. Last resort.
6. **Fallback** — say "I don't have a record of that."

**A recall that turned out wrong or stale becomes a test question — without being asked.** When Eric corrects a recalled fact, or you find that the answer you gave from recall was outdated (a newer file says otherwise), add the question to the bench yourself in the same session: one row in `~/.claude/scripts/recall-bench/questions.tsv` (set `miss`, the question as asked, the file holding the right answer, the right answer in one line), then run `CSET=miss bash ~/.claude/scripts/recall-bench/run.sh C` (~$0.06 a question) and note the result in that folder's `results.md`. Say so in one line. Eric will not remember to ask; the daily backup's recall check (`recall-bench/check.py`) then guards that question from then on.

## Daily compiled logs — read-only

`~/.claude/claude-memory-compiler/daily/{YYYY-MM-DD}.md` is produced by `claude-memory-compiler` through its own SessionEnd/PreCompact hooks, and injected by its own SessionStart hook.

- **Never hand-edit these files.** The compiler owns them.
- **Never read them eagerly.** Treat the injected snapshot as the source of truth.

## What is loaded at session start

`~/.claude/global-memory/USER.md` and `MEMORY.md` are read once at session start and are a **frozen snapshot**. Mid-session writes persist to disk but only take effect next session — this is deliberate, to preserve the prefix cache. Never load more than the startup set proactively.

## Rules

- Never exceed Tier B caps. Consolidate first.
- Always dedup before adding.
- For Tier A, the slug is the absolute cwd with every character other than a letter or digit replaced by `-` (Mac `~/DEV` → `-Users-kristinarash-DEV`, `~/.claude/skills` → `-Users-kristinarash--claude-skills`; `_` folds too: `~/DEV/CLI_Dev` → `-Users-kristinarash-DEV-CLI-Dev`, verified 2026-10-24; Windows `~/Desktop/DEV` → `C--Users-eric-rash-Desktop-DEV`; `00_Primary_Storage_Drive` → `00-Primary-Storage-Drive`). The harness injects the correct slug each session — use that, don't reconstruct it.
- **Write only to the current machine's slug.** Both machines are active as of 2026-09-10: Mac slugs are `-Users-kristinarash-*`, Windows slugs are `C--Users-eric-rash-*`. A fact written to the other machine's slug is never auto-injected here (memsearch still finds it). Durable project facts belong in the repo's `docs/` so both machines see them.
- Never announce the write mid-session beyond the one-line confirmation. The injected snapshot is frozen — the new fact appears next session, not this one.

## Verification Gate

After every write:

1. Read the exact destination back and require the intended fact to appear once in the intended tier.
2. Re-run the Tier B character cap check after the write.
3. Check the surrounding section for an unresolved contradiction or stale duplicate. Resolve it or report `FAIL`.
4. For Tier A, verify the new file has valid frontmatter and the memory index pointer resolves to it.
5. Distinguish persisted state from activation: the write can pass now, but next-session injection remains unverified until a later session observes it.

Report `PASS` only when persistence, uniqueness, tier placement, caps, and pointers are verified. Report `FAIL` with the target path and failed check otherwise. Do not emit “Saved” before read-back succeeds.

Plain code, ~1 s: BM25 keyword rank over the memsearch paths plus the whole vault, a Tier A memory first, then it opens the best file and prints the matching paragraphs with line numbers. Answer from that. If the printed paragraphs miss the answer, open the #2 or #3 candidate it lists.
3. **L2** — on `NO MATCH`, or when the words in the question are not the words in the notes: `memsearch search "query" --top-k 5`. Hybrid vector + keyword, ~1 min: the Mac Tier A slugs listed in `memory-index-paths.json` (recall.py reads every slug, Windows ones included), daily logs, transcripts, handoffs, audits.
4. **L3** — `memsearch expand <chunk_hash>`. Full markdown section around a hit.
5. **L4** — `memsearch transcript <session_id>`. Raw dialogue. Last resort.
6. **Fallback** — say "I don't have a record of that."

**A recall that turned out wrong or stale becomes a test question — without being asked.** When Eric corrects a recalled fact, or you find that the answer you gave from recall was outdated (a newer file says otherwise), add the question to the bench yourself in the same session: one row in `~/.claude/scripts/recall-bench/questions.tsv` (set `miss`, the question as asked, the file holding the right answer, the right answer in one line), then run `CSET=miss bash ~/.claude/scripts/recall-bench/run.sh C` (~$0.06 a question) and note the result in that folder's `results.md`. `~/.claude/global-memory/USER.md` and `MEMORY.md` are read once at session start and are a **frozen snapshot**. Mid-session writes persist to disk but only take effect next session — this is deliberate, to preserve the prefix cache. Never load more than the startup set proactively.

# CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

## Project Overview

**Football Player Performance Report** — a Python static HTML generator for Baylor Athletics' B.A.I.R. Initiative. Reads from three existing DuckDB pipelines, computes TSA (Total Score of Athleticism) composite scores, and renders a self-contained interactive HTML report.

**Run it:**
```bash
python generate_report.py --start 2025-09-01 --end 2026-03-28 --label "Spring 2026"
# Output: output/Spring_2026_2026-03-28.html
```

> The original React + FastAPI spec has been replaced by this approach. Reference specs are in `docs/` (TECH_SPEC.md, UI_WIREFRAMES.md, DATA_SCHEMA.md, TSA_METHODOLOGY.md) and do not reflect the implementation.

---

## Commands

```bash
pip install -r requirements.txt

# Generate a report for a date range
python generate_report.py --start YYYY-MM-DD --end YYYY-MM-DD --label "Label"

# Override output path
python generate_report.py --start 2025-09-01 --end 2026-03-28 --label "Spring 2026" --output out/custom.html

# Refresh all upstream pipelines (run before generating report)
# Wrapper script: C:/Users/eric_rash/Desktop/DEV/refresh_all_data.bat

# Individual pipeline updates:
# python C:/Users/eric_rash/Desktop/DEV/ForcePlate_DecisionSystem/src/ingest/pipeline.py
# cd C:/Users/eric_rash/Desktop/DEV/DataBase_GPS_Reporting/gps_report && python bulk_import.py --start 2025-09-01 --end <date>
# python src/perch_ingest.py --start 2025-09-01 --end <date>
```

---

## Architecture

```
generate_report.py      # CLI entry: argparse -> data -> score -> render -> write HTML
config.py               # absolute paths to all 5 data sources + output dir
src/
  data.py               # load_cmj(), load_gps(), load_bodyweight(), load_imtp(), load_perch(), merge_all()
  scorer.py             # z->t per metric, 5 domain composites, TSA, RAG
  renderer.py           # serialize DataFrame to JSON, render Jinja2 template
  perch_ingest.py       # Perch API client → data/perch.duckdb cache (run separately)
templates/
  report.html.j2        # dark-theme HTML: Chart.js radar (9 axes) + sortable table + inline JS
data/
  athlete_roster.csv    # 98 active athletes: full_name, jersey_number, position, catapult_id, forcedecks_id
  perch.duckdb          # Perch 1RM cache (not committed; populate with src/perch_ingest.py)
output/                 # generated HTML files (not committed)
```

## Data Sources

| Source | Path | Status |
|--------|------|--------|
| ForcePlate DB | `C:/Users/eric_rash/Desktop/DEV/ForcePlate_DecisionSystem/data/forceplate.db` | Built |
| GPS DB | `C:/Users/eric_rash/Desktop/DEV/DataBase_GPS_Reporting/gps_report/data/gps_history.duckdb` | Built |
| Body Weight CSV | `C:/Users/eric_rash/Desktop/DEV/Football/BodWeightWeb/BodyWeightMaster.csv` | Built |
| Roster crosswalk | `data/athlete_roster.csv` | Built |
| Perch DB | `data/perch.duckdb` (local cache, populated by `src/perch_ingest.py`) | **Built** |

**GPS pipeline note:** `bulk_import.py` imports data into the DB; `run_report.py` only generates reports from existing data — do not confuse them.

**ForcePlate DB tables used:** `raw_tests` (CMJ metrics), `classified_athletes` (mRSI + CMJ classification), `imtp_tests` (IMTP metrics). IMTP data is ingested via the ForcePlate pipeline (`ForcePlate_DecisionSystem/src/ingest/pipeline.py`).

**All paths are defined in `config.py`.** Change them there if pipelines move.

## TSA Scoring (9 axes, 5 domains)

| Domain | Metric | Source | Field |
|--------|--------|--------|-------|
| CMJ | Jump Height (cm) | `raw_tests` | `"Jump Height (Imp-Mom)"` |
| CMJ | Peak Power / BM (W/kg) | `raw_tests` | `"Peak Power / BM"` |
| CMJ | mRSI | `classified_athletes` | `mrsi` |
| GPS | High Speed Distance (m) | `athlete_sessions` | `high_speed_distance_m` |
| GPS | Player Load | `athlete_sessions` | `total_player_load` |
| GPS | Max Velocity (m/s) | `athlete_sessions` | `max_velocity_ms` |
| BW  | Body Weight (kg) | `BodyWeightMaster.csv` | WEIGHT x 0.453592 |
| Strength | Peak Force / BM (N/kg) | `imtp_tests` | `"Peak Vertical Force / BM"` |
| Weight Room | Back Squat 1RM/BW | `perch.duckdb` | 1RM (lbs) ÷ BW (lbs) |
| Weight Room | Power Clean 1RM/BW | `perch.duckdb` | 1RM (lbs) ÷ BW (lbs) |
| Weight Room | Bench Press 1RM/BW | `perch.duckdb` | 1RM (lbs) ÷ BW (lbs) |
| Weight Room | Hang Power Clean 1RM/BW | `perch.duckdb` | 1RM (lbs) ÷ BW (lbs) |

**Display-only IMTP metrics** (shown in profile panel, not in TSA domain score): Peak Force (N), RFD 0–100ms (N/s), RFD 0–200ms (N/s).

**Scoring:** z-score per metric (population = all athletes with that metric) -> t-score (z*10+50, clipped 0-100) -> domain mean (CMJ avg of 3, GPS avg of 3, BW = weight_t, Strength = peak_force_bm_t, Weight Room = mean of up to 4 exercise t-scores) -> TSA = mean of available domains (partial domain scores allowed for Weight Room).

**Weight Room radar axis:** single composite score (`weight_room_domain`); individual exercise 1RMs shown in profile panel only. Athletes without Perch data score from the remaining 4 domains; "Weight Room" shown in missing_domains note.

**RAG:** roster-relative -- top 33% green, middle 34% amber, bottom 33% red.

**Missing domain handling:** athletes missing any domain still get a TSA from available domains; a note appears in their profile panel.

## Perch API Integration (pipeline verified and data ingested 2026-04-25)

**API base:** `https://api.perch.fit` — Bearer token auth (`Authorization: Bearer <token>`).

**Ingest script:** `src/perch_ingest.py` — run before generating the report:
```bash
python src/perch_ingest.py --probe                              # verify connectivity (no dates needed)
python src/perch_ingest.py --start 2025-09-01 --end 2026-03-28 # full ingest
```

**Data source:** `POST /v3/sets` filtered by `exercise_id` — NOT `/stats` (which returns empty). 1RM is computed as `weight / pct_1rm` per set where `pct_1rm` is set (0–1 decimal). Records are newest-first; ingest stops paginating when `created_at` falls before `start_date`.

**Exercise IDs (confirmed):** Back Squat=1, Bench Press=2, Power Clean=19, Hang Power Clean=48. Defined in `_EXERCISE_ID_MAP` at top of `src/perch_ingest.py`.

**Users endpoint:** `POST /v2/users` with `{"group_id": org_id}`. Org ID resolved dynamically from `GET /v2/user` → `data.org_id` (Baylor = 959).

**Exercises tracked:** back squat, power clean, bench press, hang power clean.

**Metric:** 1RM computed from `weight / pct_1rm` per set, normalized by bodyweight (1RM ÷ BW, both lbs).

**Athlete join:** name-match from Perch `/v2/users` (first_name + last_name) to `athlete_roster.csv` full_name using `_normalize_name()`.

**API token:** stored in `.env` as `PERCH_API_TOKEN` (never committed). Copy `.env.example` → `.env` to get started.

## Scheduled pull and Parquet snapshots (Mac owns perch.duckdb)

The Mac is the only writer of `data/perch.duckdb`: launchd `com.keystone.perchpull` runs `pull_perch.sh`
(10:05 + 16:35). After a successful ingest, `pull_perch.sh` runs `export_snapshot.py` (logic in
`src/snapshot.py`), which opens the DB read-only and writes Parquet to Google Drive for Windows:

- **Where:** `$ATHLETE_SNAPSHOT_DIR/perch/`, else `00_Primary_Storage_Drive/athlete-snapshots/perch/`
  (Mac `~/Library/CloudStorage/GoogleDrive-eric.rash11@gmail.com/My Drive/...`, Windows `G:\My Drive\...`).
  `perch_1rm.parquet` + `manifest.json` (per table: rows, bytes, written_at UTC, machine, newest `test_date`).
- **Windows reads, never writes:**
  `duckdb.sql("select * from 'G:/My Drive/00_Primary_Storage_Drive/athlete-snapshots/perch/perch_1rm.parquet'")`.
- **Atomic:** written as `<table>.parquet.tmp`, then renamed.
- **Stale-writer guard:** a table whose snapshot already records more rows than this DB is refused (exit 3)
  unless `--force`. `perch_1rm` deletes and re-inserts per key, so its count never legitimately drops.
- **Failure:** exit 0 ok · 1 error · 2 no DB / Drive not mounted · 3 refused. Non-zero alerts
  (`snapshot-export exit=N`) and is recorded in `logs/last_run.json` under `snapshot_export`; the pull's
  exit code is unchanged.
- **By hand (Mac):** `.venv/bin/python export_snapshot.py --dry-run`, then without `--dry-run`.

## Athlete Roster

`data/athlete_roster.csv` is the join key between all three pipelines. **Do not delete it.**

- 98 active athletes; all have ForcePlate data
- 83 also have a Catapult GPS ID; 15 are not yet in Catapult
- Jersey numbers are mostly blank -- fill manually for UI display
- Joins: ForcePlate on `forcedecks_id`, GPS on `catapult_id`, BW on normalized `full_name`

To add new athletes or update IDs, edit `data/athlete_roster.csv` directly.

## What Is Not Yet Built

See [CONTEXT.md](CONTEXT.md) for full detail. Key deferred items:

- **Perch / Weight Room domain** -- Fully implemented (2026-04-24). Run `src/perch_ingest.py --probe` first time to verify API field names, then full ingest. Once `data/perch.duckdb` is populated the Weight Room domain activates automatically.
- **Dual y-axes in trend detail charts** -- RFD (N/s) and Peak Force/BM (N/kg) share a single y-axis; add secondary axis when Chart.js dual-axis is wired up
- **Athlete comparison panel** -- side-by-side spider chart overlay
- **BW fallback** -- Fully implemented (2026-04-25). `_load_fd_bw()` and `_load_bw_combined()` in `src/data.py` fill gaps using `"Bodyweight in Kilograms"` from `raw_tests`. CSV wins; FD fills NaN. Wired into `merge_all()`, `load_perch()`, `load_perch_history()`.
- **Position-specific normalization** -- v1 uses full-roster z-scores
- **Jersey numbers** -- need manual entry in `data/athlete_roster.csv`

## Downstream Projects

**Risk_Stratification_Engine** (`C:/Users/eric_rash/Desktop/DEV/Risk_Stratification_Engine/`) reads the same canonical DB files. Its `config/paths.local.yaml` already points to the correct paths. Run `refresh_all_data.bat` to update data for both projects simultaneously.

## Git Conventions

- Branches: `main` (stable) -> `dev` (active) -> `feature/*`
- Commit prefixes: `feat:`, `fix:`, `refactor:`, `data:`, `docs:`
- `.gitignore` excludes: `__pycache__/`, `venv/`, `.env`, `data/*.duckdb`, `data/raw/`

# Risk Stratification Engine

## Development Workflow
- Use TDD (test-driven development) for all feature implementations
- After implementing features, run the full test suite and verify all tests pass before committing
- Commit and push changes with descriptive messages after completing each logical unit of work
- Update relevant documentation (CLAUDE.md, session.md, README) as part of the same commit

## Pipelines

### Long-Running Processes
- When running long Python pipelines or backfills in the background, use `python -u` or set `PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1` so output is visible
- Add explicit progress logging (every N records) for any pipeline expected to take >1 minute
- For VALD/external API calls, implement retry-with-backoff and a watchdog timeout to avoid silent hangs

## Agent Delegation Guardrails
- When delegating to parallel sub-agents, verify their output against source material (e.g., extract text directly from PDFs to check citations) — agents have hallucinated authors and assigned wrong IDs in past sessions
- Ensure sub-agents have necessary Write permissions configured before launching parallel work
- Set explicit watchdog timeouts and assume any stalled agent may have already written valid partial output worth recovering
