# Status

## Current state
Running daily on Eric's MacBook since 2026-10-16 (macOS 27.0.1 as of 2026-10-24): daemon,
`ev` CLI and menu-bar app, signed with the local certificate, Full Disk Access on. CI (macOS 15
runners) is the compiler and is green on `main` (51 tests at d2b8ccc). Detail of the first
real-Mac day:
`docs/handoffs/2026-10-16-real-mac-and-ui.md`.

2026-10-24: cloud folders are no longer indexed (`~/Library/CloudStorage`, `~/Library/Mobile
Documents`, `~/Library/Application Support/FileProvider`; see `docs/DECISIONS.md`). The daemon
had written about 27,000 "giving up ... Resource deadlock avoided" lines (5.5 MB) to
`~/Library/Logs/everythingd.log` re-listing them. New daemon and `ev` installed (not the app,
see Gotchas) and `ev --rescan` run: 3.21M entries for `/` (was 4.10M; 887K were cloud, so Full
Disk Access still holds), full scan 122 s, 0 entries left under the three folders. The old log was kept as history (27,706 lines
before the restart). No "giving up" lines from the restart (06:12 UTC) to 06:21 UTC, and live
updates kept applying. The old failures came in bursts with quiet hours between, so recheck
with `grep -c "giving up" ~/Library/Logs/everythingd.log` (27,195 on 2026-10-24) after a day.

Search window, all confirmed on the Mac: scope menu (All, This Mac, Cloud, each drive), file-type
menu (Everything's filters), "Show temp files" toggle (temp hidden by default), header sorting,
right-click column chooser, drag to reorder, default columns Name | Type | Path.
Scope menu also lists each cloud account (Google Drive, OneDrive, Dropbox, Box per
~/Library/CloudStorage folder, plus iCloud Drive) under Cloud, added 2026-10-16: built and
query-checked on the Mac with `ev`, window not yet seen. Detail:
`docs/handoffs/2026-10-16-cloud-account-scopes.md`. Since 2026-10-24 those scopes return
nothing unless the account is added as a location (Next #1). Until the app is rebuilt, add it in
config.json `extraRoots`, not the Locations window: the installed 2026-10-16 app still uses the
old exclusions and answers "Already indexed: ... is inside /". The daemon's 30 s location check
picks up a config.json change on its own.

| Measured on CI, 1.35M entries | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Plain, wildcard, ext, size searches | 2 to 15 ms |
| `path:` / `regex:` searches | 16 to 30 ms / 6 to 46 ms |
| `video:`, `doc: report` | 16 to 22 ms |
| `report !temp:` (first search, builds the mask) | 43 ms; later searches only extend it |

## Next
1. Scope menu: offer a cloud account (and Cloud) only when it is indexed, that is, added as a
   location; `SearchScope.choices` lists every ~/Library/CloudStorage folder today. Small change
   plus a test tweak.
2. The menu-bar app no longer builds on this Mac (Gotchas): install full Xcode, or wait for
   Command Line Tools that ship SwiftUIMacros. Until then `scripts/install.sh` stops at
   `make-app.sh`; the installed 2026-10-16 app keeps running.
3. On the Mac: Locations window (menu bar > Locations…), live updates (create, rename, delete a
   file and check `ev`), unplug and replug CRASHBOX. Rest of the #2 checklist.
4. Post the real-Mac numbers on #3 and close it (GitHub MCP was down at the end of 2026-10-16).
5. Delete the `codex-review` and `codex-review-base` branches on GitHub, close #10.
6. Optional: folders that each take exactly 6.0 s to list (once OneDrive; in the 2026-10-24
   scan, sandbox folders under ~/Library/Containers); Type column sorting.

## Open questions
- None. #9 decided 2026-10-16: keep building (see `docs/DECISIONS.md`).

## Gotchas
- On the Mac, `swift test` fails with "no such module 'XCTest'" (no full Xcode). Build locally,
  let CI run the tests.
- Since macOS 27 / Swift 6.4 Command Line Tools (2026-10-24), plain `swift build` fails in
  EverythingApp: "plugin for module 'SwiftUIMacros' not found" (it ships only with Xcode).
  `swift build -c release --product everythingd` (and `--product ev`) still work.
- Daemon-only install while the app cannot build: copy `.build/release/everythingd` to
  `build/`, sign it with `codesign --force --options runtime --sign "MacEverything Local
  Signing" --identifier com.erash11.maceverything.daemon`, check `codesign -d -r-` matches the
  installed binary (same requirement keeps Full Disk Access), move the old
  `~/.local/bin/everythingd` aside, copy the new one in, then
  `launchctl kickstart -k gui/$(id -u)/com.erash11.maceverything.daemon`. Same for `ev`
  (identifier com.erash11.maceverything.ev, no restart). On 2026-10-24 the kickstart killed the
  old daemon mid-save (exit -9), launchd then reported last exit reason OS_REASON_CODESIGNING,
  and the new daemon logged "starting" 18 s after the kickstart and ran fine.
- No Swift toolchain in Claude cloud sessions: CI is the compiler. When the GitHub MCP is down,
  `curl https://api.github.com/repos/erash11/MacEverything/actions/runs` and
  `.../actions/jobs/<id>/logs` work without auth (public repo).
- Cloud sessions cannot delete GitHub branches (API and `git push --delete` both refused).
- Index writes must stay on `IndexService.work`; `PathTable` and the temp mask rely on parent id
  < child id and on records being append-only.
- External drives with no FSEvents history (CRASHBOX reports event id 0, likely exFAT) are

name: aios-audit
description: >-
  Audit the whole AI operating system across decay tiers - skills, agents,

  and Pi - then propose exactly two next builds. Use when the user says

# AIOS Audit — is the harness itself still true?

agent memory, and parity between Claude Code, Codex, and Pi. For every other
layer it **delegates**; it never re-implements another audit.

|---|---|
| `os-audit` (project) | project data: routing, index truth, freshness, duplication |
| `brain-audit` | SecondBrain as a system — the four C's |
| `improve-system` | note-level rot: stale seeds, duplicates, conflicts |

is cheap; a deletion is not.

install), `pool_third_party`, `codex_third_party` (deliberately preserved installs).

For each due layer, invoke the owner named in `rot.md`, **read-only**:

- Say it plainly in the invocation: *report findings only; apply nothing, write no
  ledger, create no files.*
- `improve-system` applies previously approved proposals in its own Step 0 —
  suppress that explicitly. `brain-audit` appends to its own trend table — suppress

  Claude-only evidence. First check Codex:

output**.

with this report.

Ranked. Each with the one command or sentence that starts it. Not ten. Two.

**Monthly nudge**
```
User: "audit my AI OS"
→ reads rot.md: Skills and Rules past due, Hooks inside its window
```

Not "how often did I run it?" but **"would the current model do this fine
without the skill?"** If yes, the skill is a crutch that now limits the model.
Delete it. Keep only skills carrying tacit knowledge the model cannot know:
force-plate thresholds, GPS conventions, Baylor reporting norms, Eric's own
routines.

Seasonal skills (`forecast-capture`, `ingest-book`) are exempt from low-use
pressure. Judge them in season.

## Delegation contract (R2-09)

A delegate is invoked **read-only**, for a **named scope**, and its receipt is
written **only** for the scope it actually covered.

1. **Read-only.** Before invoking a delegate, instruct it explicitly: report
   findings, apply nothing, write no ledger, create no files. Several delegates
   (`improve-system` among them) begin by applying previously approved proposals
   — that must be suppressed. `aios-audit` writes only its own report and the
   `Last audited` column.
2. **Scope must be verified, not assumed.** A delegate's actual coverage is what
   its body scans, not what this table wishes it scanned. `improve-system` scans
   `~/SecondBrain/` — Notes, Knowledge, Projects. It does **not** touch
   `~/.claude/projects/*/memory/` or `global-memory/`. Those are audited by
   `aios-audit` directly.
3. **A receipt covers only what was checked.** If a delegate returns findings for
   a narrower scope than its row claims, write the date **and** a scope note, or
   leave the row `unknown`. Never stamp a date because a delegate exited cleanly.

- `~/.claude/skills/` is canonical, is a git repo, and contains **no TRACKED symlinks**
  (`git ls-files -s` shows no mode 120000). On-disk links to third-party skills are
  expected; they are listed in the per-machine `.git/info/exclude` (never the tracked
  `.gitignore`), and a pre-commit hook refuses to commit one. What must never happen is
  committing a link, because Windows pulls this repo and a Mac link is dead there.
- `~/.agents/skills/` and `~/.codex/skills/` are **generated views**. Each carries
  a `.generated-by-sync-to-codex` manifest. Every entry **in the manifest** must be
  a symlink on Mac (a copy on Windows); wrong representation is drift.
- Entries **not** in the manifest are third-party installs (`npx skills add`).
  They are counted and reported, **never** flagged as errors and never pruned.
- Support directories (`_shared/`) have no SKILL.md and must never be pruned.

## Direction of travel

**Fewer skills, stricter rules.** Skills get deleted; rules get sharpened.

## Cadence

Monthly metrics: launchd `com.keystone.aiosaudit`, day 1 at 14:00.
It writes a trend row and a nudge. It does not commit and does not push.
The agentic audit is run by hand: "audit my AI OS" in `~/DEV/KeystoneOS`.

toolUseResult.originalFile:
# CREDENTIALS.md — key inventory for machine restore

**This file contains NO secret values and must never contain any.** It records *which*
keys each project needs and *where to reissue them*, so a restored machine can be made
functional without guesswork. Values live in your password manager and in the issuing
service's console — nowhere else, by design.

Generated 2026-08-03 by reading key names from `.env` / `.env.example` files. Tracked in
`dotclaude`; mirrored to the SSD.

> **Why this exists.** Every backup correctly excludes credentials. The consequence, found
> during the 2026-08-03 migration audit, is that a perfect restore produces code that
> cannot run and no record of what is missing. This is that record.

## Restore order

Do these in the order you need them, not all at once. Items 1–3 unblock the daily cadence;
the rest can wait until you next touch that project.

| # | Project | File to create | Keys | Reissue from |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | ~~`morning-briefing`~~ | ~~`secrets/gmail_credentials.json`~~ | ~~OAuth client JSON~~ | **RETIRED 2026-08-14** — project removed from disk, local `secrets/` destroyed. Only needed if re-cloned from `github.com/erash11/morning-briefing` |
| 2 | ~~`morning-briefing`~~ | ~~`secrets/gmail_token.json`~~ | ~~generated, not copied~~ | **RETIRED 2026-08-14** — see row 1 |
| 3 | `DataBase_GPS_Reporting/gps_report` | `.env` | `CATAPULT_TOKEN` | Catapult OpenField → account settings → API token |
| 4 | `ForcePlate_DecisionSystem` | `.env` | `VALD_CLIENT_ID`, `VALD_CLIENT_SECRET`, `VALD_REGION_URL`, `VALD_TEAM_ID` | VALD Hub → API access. Region URL is tenant-specific — copy exactly |
| 5 | `Football/PFF_Data_Project` | `.env` | `PFF_BASE_URL`, `PFF_API_KEY`, `BAYLOR_TEAM_ID` | PFF Ultimate account rep. **Institutional — tied to Baylor's contract** |
| 6 | `PlayerProfiles_FB_03-28-2026` | `.env` | `PERCH_API_TOKEN` | Perch dashboard → integrations |
| 7 | `reMarkale_extract` | `.env` | `GOOGLE_VISION_API_KEY`, `GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT` | Google Cloud Console → Vision API |
| 8 | `Football/FaceComps/simulator` | `.env.local` | `DATABASE_URL`, `SITE_PASSWORD`, `COOKIE_SECRET`, `CATAPULT_TOKEN` | Supabase → project settings → database. `COOKIE_SECRET` is self-generated (`openssl rand -hex 32`) |
| 9 | `CFB_Victory_Model` | `.env` | `CFBD_API_KEY` | collegefootballdata.com → free API key |
| 10 | `KeystoneOS/zotero-photo-capture` | `.env` | `ZOTERO_API_KEY`, `ZOTERO_USER_ID`, `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `CROSSREF_MAILTO` | Zotero → Settings → Feeds/API. `CROSSREF_MAILTO` is just your email |
| 11 | ~~`morning-briefing` (email delivery)~~ | ~~`~/.config/morning-briefing/env` (0600)~~ | ~~`GMAIL_APP_PASSWORD`~~ | **RETIRED 2026-08-14 — no longer OUTSTANDING.** Was an open item (briefing generated but did not email until set); moot now the project is retired. Revoke the app password at myaccount.google.com/apppasswords if one was ever created |

## OAuth connectors — no files, re-auth in the app

These re-authenticate through a browser prompt on first use. Nothing to restore, but
expect to sign in to each once:

Fireflies · Google Drive · Gmail · Google Calendar · Microsoft 365 (Baylor) · Supabase ·
Vercel · Zotero · reMarkable · Anthropic (Claude Code) · OpenAI (Codex) · GitHub (`gh auth login`)

## Which of these survive leaving Baylor

| Survives | Does not |
|---|---|
| CFBD, Zotero, Anthropic, OpenAI, GitHub, Google (personal), reMarkable, Supabase, Vercel | PFF (Baylor contract), Catapult (Baylor tenant), VALD (Baylor tenant), Perch (Baylor tenant), Microsoft 365 |

Institutional keys stop working when the contract or your account does. That is expected
and correct — do not attempt to preserve them. The *code* that uses them is yours; the
*access* is Baylor's.

## Known live issue

**2026-08-03 — Outlook auth for `morning-briefing` is expired.** The 08:19 brief sent with
0 email threads. Reauthenticate rather than carrying this into the migration:

```powershell
& "$env:USERPROFILE\Desktop\DEV\morning-briefing\scripts\reauth.bat"
```

On macOS this script needs porting to `.sh` — see `MIGRATION-MACOS.md` Step 8.

## Accepted exception — credential files on the transport drive (expanded 2026-08-05)

**Decided by Eric, 2026-08-05, with the exposure stated.** After the macOS restore
surfaced that the drive carries SIX live credential files (not one), Eric chose to
KEEP all of them on the drive rather than delete after restoring:

- `DEV-nonrepo/Football/FaceComps/simulator/.env.local` (the original 2026-08-04 exception)
- `DEV-repo-data/ForcePlate_DecisionSystem/.env` (4 VALD keys)
- `DEV-repo-data/PlayerProfiles_FB_03-28-2026/.env` (Perch token)
- `DEV-repo-data/DataBase_GPS_Reporting/gps_report/.env` (Catapult token)
- `DEV-nonrepo/reMarkale_extract/.env` (Google Vision key)
- `DEV-nonrepo/Football/PFF_Data_Project/.env` (PFF keys)

Consequences, restated: the drive is unencrypted exFAT — anyone who plugs it in can
read these values. If the drive is lost or leaves your control, rotate everything
above at the issuing services. The ported backup's deny-list prevents any NEW
credential from reaching the drive; these six are grandfathered by this decision.

## Superseded — original FaceComps-only exception

**Decided by Eric, 2026-08-04, with the exposure stated.** `D:\AssistantBackup\DEV-nonrepo\Football\FaceComps\simulator\.env.local`
remains on the external drive, holding live values for `DATABASE_URL`, `SITE_PASSWORD`,
`COOKIE_SECRET`, and `CATAPULT_TOKEN`.

This is the one deliberate departure from "no credentials in any backup." The reasoning
was that the old machine — the only other copy — is being decommissioned during the
2026-08-04 migration, so purging risked losing the values outright.

Consequences, recorded so they are not rediscovered by surprise:

- The drive is unencrypted NTFS. Anyone who plugs it in can read these four values.
- If the drive is lost, checked as luggage, or left unattended, rotate all four:
  Supabase (`DATABASE_URL`), the site password, and the Catapult token. `COOKIE_SECRET`
  needs no service — regenerate with `openssl rand -hex 32`.
- Once these values are in the password manager, delete the SSD copy and remove this
  section. The backup script's deny-list already prevents it being re-copied, so deleting
  it is permanent and safe.

Every other credential found on the drive was purged on 2026-08-04: `morning-briefing/secrets/owa-profile`
(7,633 files — a live authenticated Outlook browser profile with Cookies and Login Data)
and an `edge-profile` under `SpecialRequests` (272 files). Both were session state that
re-authentication regenerates.

## Rules

1. **Never** commit a value to this file or any repo. `.env` files stay gitignored.
2. When you add a project that needs a key, add a row here in the same session.
3. `gmail_token.json` and any other *generated* token is regenerated, never restored — a
   restored token is usually already expired and fails confusingly.
4. If a key leaks, rotate it at the issuing service first, then update your password
   manager. This file needs no change; it names keys, not values.

def main():
    global LOG_DATE_OVERRIDE

    if len(sys.argv) < 3:
        logging.error("Usage: %s <context_file.md> <session_id> [YYYY-MM-DD]", sys.argv[0])
        sys.exit(1)

    context_file = Path(sys.argv[1])
    session_id = sys.argv[2]

    # Optional backfill date: recover a stranded context file into its own day's log.
    if len(sys.argv) > 3 and sys.argv[3]:
        try:
            datetime.strptime(sys.argv[3], "%Y-%m-%d")
        except ValueError:
            logging.error("Bad backfill date %r, expected YYYY-MM-DD", sys.argv[3])
            sys.exit(1)
        LOG_DATE_OVERRIDE = sys.argv[3]
        logging.info("Backfill mode: writing to daily log %s", LOG_DATE_OVERRIDE)

    logging.info("flush.py started for session %s, context: %s", session_id, context_file)

    if not context_file.exists():
        logging.error("Context file not found: %s", context_file)
        return

    # Deduplication: skip if same session was flushed within 60 seconds
    state = load_flush_state()
    if (
        state.get("session_id") == session_id
        and time.time() - state.get("timestamp", 0) < 60
    ):
        logging.info("Skipping duplicate flush for session %s", session_id)
        context_file.unlink(missing_ok=True)
        return

    # Read pre-extracted context
    context = context_file.read_text(encoding="utf-8").strip()
    if not context:
        logging.info("Context file is empty, skipping")
        context_file.unlink(missing_ok=True)
        return

    logging.info("Flushing session %s: %d chars", session_id, len(context))

    # Run the LLM extraction
    response = asyncio.run(run_flush(context))

    # Append to daily log
    if "FLUSH_OK" in response:
        logging.info("Result: FLUSH_OK")
        append_to_daily_log(
            "FLUSH_OK - Nothing worth saving from this session", "Memory Flush"
        )
    elif "FLUSH_ERROR" in response:
        logging.error("Result: %s", response)
        append_to_daily_log(response, "Memory Flush")
        escalate_flush_error(response, session_id)
    else:
        logging.info("Result: saved to daily log (%d chars)", len(response))
        append_to_daily_log(response, "Session")

    # Update dedup state
    save_flush_state({"session_id": session_id, "timestamp": time.time()})

    # Clean up context file
    context_file.unlink(missing_ok=True)

    # End-of-day auto-compilation: if it's past the compile hour and today's
    # log hasn't been compiled yet, trigger compile.py in the background.
    maybe_trigger_compilation()

    logging.info("Flush complete for session %s", session_id)

"""Regression test: a failed flush must keep the session context, not delete it
(audit mp-flush-error-deletes-context: the 10-21 ENOTFOUND flush lost its context).

Run: uv run python scripts/test_flush_error_keeps_context.py
"""

import sys
import tempfile
import types
from pathlib import Path

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).parent))

# flush imports the Agent SDK at module load; this test never calls it.
fake = types.ModuleType("claude_agent_sdk")
for name in ("AssistantMessage", "ClaudeAgentOptions", "ResultMessage", "TextBlock"):
    setattr(fake, name, type(name, (), {"__init__": lambda self, *a, **k: None}))
fake.query = None
sys.modules["claude_agent_sdk"] = fake

import flush  # noqa: E402

with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as d:
    d = Path(d)
    flush.STRANDED_DIR = d / "_stranded-archive"
    calls = []
    flush.append_to_daily_log = lambda text, section: calls.append(("log", section))
    flush.escalate_flush_error = lambda resp, sid: calls.append(("escalate", sid))
    flush.save_flush_state = lambda s: calls.append(("state", s))
    flush.load_flush_state = lambda: {}
    flush.maybe_trigger_compilation = lambda: calls.append(("compile",))

    async def fail(context):
        return "FLUSH_ERROR: ResultError: API Error: Can't reach the API server (ENOTFOUND)"

    flush.run_flush = fail
    ctx = d / "session-flush-abc-20261021-201619.md"
    ctx.write_text("context that must survive", encoding="utf-8")
    sys.argv = ["flush.py", str(ctx), "abc"]
    flush.main()

    kept = flush.STRANDED_DIR / ctx.name
    assert not ctx.exists(), "context file left in place"
    assert kept.exists() and kept.read_text(encoding="utf-8") == "context that must survive", "context not kept"
    assert ("escalate", "abc") in calls, "error not escalated"
    assert not any(c[0] == "state" for c in calls), "dedup stamp written on error (a retry would be skipped)"

    # A failed backfill of a kept file leaves it where it is.
    sys.argv = ["flush.py", str(kept), "abc", "2026-10-21"]
    flush.main()
    assert kept.exists(), "kept file lost on a failed backfill"
    assert len(list(flush.STRANDED_DIR.iterdir())) == 1, "failed backfill made a second copy"

    # Success still deletes the context, as before.
    async def ok(context):
        return "FLUSH_OK"

    flush.run_flush = ok
    ctx2 = d / "session-flush-def-20261024-090000.md"
    ctx2.write_text("fine", encoding="utf-8")
    sys.argv = ["flush.py", str(ctx2), "def"]
    flush.main()
    assert not ctx2.exists() and not (flush.STRANDED_DIR / ctx2.name).exists(), "success path changed"

print("test_flush_error_keeps_context: all checks passed")

# 2026-10-24 — Agent-file cleanup (FILE-ORGANIZATION-PLAN Task 9)

Mac, Opus. Started as "have we audited the Claude system?", became "fix everything" (Eric
pre-approved decisions; mid-season freeze lifted).

## What was done

Rules for every kind of agent file: `~/.claude/STORAGE.md` → "Agent files". Plan entry:
`docs/FILE-ORGANIZATION-PLAN.md` Task 9.

- **Hooks:** `~/.codex/hooks` → symlink to `~/.claude/hooks` (ends the two-copies trap);
  unwired LIFEOS hook files and `hooks/lib`, `hooks/handlers` removed. Metric
  `hooks_codex_is_link` in `KeystoneOS/scripts/aios-metrics.py`.
- **LIFEOS retired:** `~/.claude/LIFEOS` and `~/.config/LIFEOS` parked in `~/_PARKED_COPIES/`
  (only copies); ArXiv, Science, ISA skills no longer point at it; `lifeos` alias and bun PATH
  removed from `~/.zshrc`.
- **Search and memory:** `harvest-dev-docs.sh` is a true mirror and never mirrors local-only,
  health or confidential repos (52 folders parked); roots now include `~/DEV/docs/handoffs`,
  `global-memory/handoffs`, `~/.claude/audits`; `recall.py` dedupes `.windows.md` twins (eval
  21/30 unchanged); 8 Tier A `_` slugs folded to `-` (31 memory files had never loaded); one
  append-only `.errors-ledger.log`; RTP athlete memory de-identified.
- **daily-backup.ps1:** log trims (not `permission-gate/shadow.jsonl`), `codex-config.tgz`,
  `shell-dotfiles.tgz` (refuses a file that looks like it holds a secret), `auth.json` never to
  the SSD, index logging and died-mid-index check, daily `uv cache prune` (locked = skip).
  Offline test `~/.claude/scripts/test_daily_backup.ps1`: ALL PASS.
- **RESTORE.md:** rewritten for the Mac, fact-checked against the live machine; START-HERE,
  MIGRATION-MACOS, RECOVERY-INVENTORY, restore.command retired (git history keeps them).
- **Repos:** `~/DEV/drive-tools` (new, private) holds the Drive index tools moved out of
  `_INBOX`; CLI_Dev run state untracked; graphify-out baselines dropped; KeystoneOS `jobs.json`
  lists all 15 launchd jobs (inventory rows never auto-run); `projects.json` has no dead paths.
- **Removed:** Cloudroom and Grok Bot (Eric), 16 disabled plugins, 2 marketplaces, dead tool
  homes, 65 dead skillOverrides, loose `.bak` copies. playwright and claude-mem-cowork off.
- **Code fixes:** Windows `C:/` paths in PlayerProfiles, Risk engine, ForcePlate research,
  SpringPlayerEvals (tests pass; a full player report builds); skill-router hook guarded (a
  missing `router.py` blocked every prompt); `flush.py` keeps the context on FLUSH_ERROR;
  everythingd excludes Drive/iCloud/FileProvider (0 "giving up" lines since).

## Eric only (security settings, accounts, secrets)

1. Firewall on: `sudo /usr/libexec/ApplicationFirewall/socketfilterfw --setglobalstate on`
2. Empty the Trash when ready (about 4 GB: names end `-2026-10-23` / `-2026-10-24`).
3. claude.ai plugin settings: turn off the synced duplicates (superpowers 6.4.2,
   desktop-commander, browser-use — 7 browser-use servers hold the uv cache lock).
4. Antigravity: in `~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/settings.json` set `toolPermission` to ask and
   `allowNonWorkspaceAccess` to false (it runs with no dcg guard).
5. Rotate the EXA and Firecrawl keys in `~/.claude/skills-archive/2026-09-12/web-scraping/.env`.
6. Revoke the Grok Bot device on xAI's side.
7. Decide whether to purge from git history: the old RTP athlete memory (dotclaude) and the
   4 raw session files (claude-memory-compiler). Both repos are private; current files are clean.
8. Time Machine: needs a spare disk (CRASHBOX is exFAT and serves the SSD backup layer).

## Left open (not urgent)

- MacEverything menu-bar app no longer builds on macOS 27 Command Line Tools (needs Xcode);
  scope menu still shows cloud accounts that now return nothing.
- `~/.credentials.json` (Oct 8) may be unused on the Mac; check after a sign-out/in.
- DEV Task 4 (Area folders) stays a planned multi-sitting move.
- About 90 medium/low findings from the 10-22 audit remain in
  `~/.claude/audits/2026-10-22-system-audit-findings.md`.

"""Regression test: a failed flush must keep the session context, not delete it
(audit mp-flush-error-deletes-context: the 10-21 ENOTFOUND flush lost its context).

Run: uv run python scripts/test_flush_error_keeps_context.py
"""

import sys
import tempfile
import types
from pathlib import Path

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).parent))

# flush imports the Agent SDK at module load; this test never calls it.
fake = types.ModuleType("claude_agent_sdk")
for name in ("AssistantMessage", "ClaudeAgentOptions", "ResultMessage", "TextBlock"):
    setattr(fake, name, type(name, (), {"__init__": lambda self, *a, **k: None}))
fake.query = None
sys.modules["claude_agent_sdk"] = fake

import os, tempfile  # noqa: E402
os.environ["FLUSH_LOG_FILE"] = os.path.join(tempfile.mkdtemp(), "flush.log")  # keep the live log clean
import flush  # noqa: E402

with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as d:
    d = Path(d)
    flush.STRANDED_DIR = d / "_stranded-archive"
    calls = []
    flush.append_to_daily_log = lambda text, section: calls.append(("log", section))
    flush.escalate_flush_error = lambda resp, sid: calls.append(("escalate", sid))
    flush.save_flush_state = lambda s: calls.append(("state", s))
    flush.load_flush_state = lambda: {}
    flush.maybe_trigger_compilation = lambda: calls.append(("compile",))

    async def fail(context):
        return "FLUSH_ERROR: ResultError: API Error: Can't reach the API server (ENOTFOUND)"

    flush.run_flush = fail
    ctx = d / "session-flush-abc-20261021-201619.md"
    ctx.write_text("context that must survive", encoding="utf-8")
    sys.argv = ["flush.py", str(ctx), "abc"]
    flush.main()

    kept = flush.STRANDED_DIR / ctx.name
    assert not ctx.exists(), "context file left in place"
    assert kept.exists() and kept.read_text(encoding="utf-8") == "context that must survive", "context not kept"
    assert ("escalate", "abc") in calls, "error not escalated"
    assert not any(c[0] == "state" for c in calls), "dedup stamp written on error (a retry would be skipped)"

    # A failed backfill of a kept file leaves it where it is.
    sys.argv = ["flush.py", str(kept), "abc", "2026-10-21"]
    flush.main()
    assert kept.exists(), "kept file lost on a failed backfill"
    assert len(list(flush.STRANDED_DIR.iterdir())) == 1, "failed backfill made a second copy"

    # Success still deletes the context, as before.
    async def ok(context):
        return "FLUSH_OK"

    flush.run_flush = ok
    ctx2 = d / "session-flush-def-20261024-090000.md"
    ctx2.write_text("fine", encoding="utf-8")
    sys.argv = ["flush.py", str(ctx2), "def"]
    flush.main()
    assert not ctx2.exists() and not (flush.STRANDED_DIR / ctx2.name).exists(), "success path changed"

print("test_flush_error_keeps_context: all checks passed")

It was not version skew. `allowed_tools=[]` is only an auto-approve list, so the flush model had every built-in tool plus 162 MCP tools. In all 3 failed transcripts it acted on requests inside the pasted conversation (Read, Bash, a Drive search) and spent both turns on tool calls. - 2026-10-12 (Mac): upgraded `claude-agent-sdk` 0.2.152 → 0.2.165 to test whether version skew causes the "Reached maximum number of turns (2)" flush failures. Committed as `4395af3`; merged the Windows WMI flush fix (`e00b378`) and pushed as `d677595`. The import is verified. The fix is NOT proven until a session end writes `FLUSH_OK`.

  `uv lock --check`, `uv sync`, then proved an end-to-end flush completes on 0.2.152 BEFORE
  merging to `main`.

  `daily/2026-09-16.md`. One produced real content; the other returned `FLUSH_OK`
  ("nothing worth saving"). Originals kept in `leftover-backup-2026-09-19/`.

- `daily/` and `leftover-backup-*/` are gitignored on purpose - raw session context stays off
  GitHub. That means they reach backup ONLY via the SSD, so while CRASHBOX is unplugged they
  exist in one place. Do not "fix" this by tracking them.

  writes a `### Memory Flush` section rather than a `### Session` one. Grepping for
  `^### Session` alone will make a successful flush look like it vanished.

skills.name: memory-write
skills.content:
Base directory for this skill: /Users/kristinarash/.claude/skills/memory-write

# Memory Write

## Outcome
- Fact added to, updated in, or removed from the correct memory tier
- Tier-B caps enforced (2,500 chars for MEMORY.md, 1,375 for USER.md)
- Confirmation: "Saved — will be active from next session."

## Pick the tier first

Ask: "Will this fact still be true and useful in 3 months, across multiple projects?"

**Tier A — `~/.claude/projects/<slug>/memory/`** (one file per fact, indexed by MEMORY.md)
- Durable user facts → `user_*.md` (metadata.type: user)
- Stable project conventions / gotchas → `project_*.md` (metadata.type: project)
- Behavioral feedback rules → `feedback_*.md` (metadata.type: feedback)
- External-system pointers → `reference_*.md` (metadata.type: reference)

**Tier B — `~/.claude/global-memory/`** (single capped file)
- Active threads (in-progress work) → `MEMORY.md` `## Active Threads`
- Current env notes (URLs, tool versions, project structure in play) → `MEMORY.md` `## Environment Notes`
- Pending decisions → `MEMORY.md` `## Pending Decisions`
- Durable user profile updates → `USER.md`

## Steps

1. **Decide tier** using the rule above.
2. **Read** the target file in full.
3. **Dedup check** — substring scan; if the fact already exists, skip or update in place.
4. **Cap check** for Tier B — `wc -c < ~/.claude/global-memory/MEMORY.md` (or USER.md). If over cap, consolidate (merge similar entries, prune stale) before adding.
5. **Write** the change.
   - Tier A: create a new file with proper frontmatter (name, description, metadata.type) and add a one-line pointer to that slug's `MEMORY.md` index. `name:` follows the rule below. Do it in one call, from the project folder (the slug comes from the current folder; `--dir` overrides):
     `python3 ~/.claude/scripts/remember.py --type <t> --name <bare-slug> --desc "<one line>" --hook "<when to open>" [--why "..." --how "..."] "<fact>"`
     It checks the name rule, refuses an existing or look-alike name (exit 2: read that file, then `--update` it or `--force`), writes the file and the index line, runs steps 1 and 4 of the Verification Gate, and refreshes recall.py's index. `PASS` covers those checks; step 3 (contradictions) is still yours.
   - Tier B: append under the correct `##` section.
6. **Confirm** in one line: `Saved — will be active from next session.`

## The `name:` field — bare kebab slug

**`name:` = the filename stem minus its leading type token, kebab-cased.** The type
already lives in `metadata.type` and the filename already carries the prefix; repeating
it in `name:` is the third copy.

| File | `name:` |
|---|---|
| `project_automation-cadence.md` | `automation-cadence` |
| `user_sports-teams.md` | `sports-teams` |
| `reference_baylor-house-style.md` | `baylor-house-style` |
| `feedback_project_idea_capture.md` | `project-idea-capture` |

Note the last row: strip only the **leading** token. `feedback_project_idea_capture.md`
is a feedback memory *about* project-idea capture — its name keeps the word `project`.

`[[links]]` target this bare name, never the filename and never a prefixed variant.

This rule exists because it was previously unwritten: an audit on 2026-09-02 found the
corpus split 59 bare / 58 prefixed, which broke 37 links. Both forms look right in
isolation, so without a stated rule the split regrows on every write.

## Actions

- **add** — append (default)
- **replace** — substring match + swap. Preferred over add when updating an existing fact.
- **remove** — confirm with the user before deleting.

## Retrieval — the tiered ladder

When the user asks about past context, decisions, or "did we already…?", climb in order and stop as soon as the question is answered. Do not run a search when the answer is already in the injected snapshot.

1. **Tier 0** — scan what is already in context (USER.md, MEMORY.md, today's compiled log). Zero cost.
2. **L1** — `python3 ~/.claude/scripts/recall.py "question"`. Plain code, ~1 s: BM25 keyword rank over the memsearch paths plus the whole vault, a Tier A memory first, then it opens the best file and prints the matching paragraphs with line numbers. Answer from that. If the printed paragraphs miss the answer, open the #2 or #3 candidate it lists.
3. **L2** — on `NO MATCH`, or when the words in the question are not the words in the notes: `memsearch search "query" --top-k 5`. Hybrid vector + keyword, ~1 min: Tier A files (including the Windows-machine slugs), daily logs, transcripts.
4. **L3** — `memsearch expand <chunk_hash>`. Full markdown section around a hit.
5. **L4** — `memsearch transcript <session_id>`. Raw dialogue. Last resort.
6. **Fallback** — say "I don't have a record of that."

**A recall that turned out wrong or stale becomes a test question — without being asked.** When Eric corrects a recalled fact, or you find that the answer you gave from recall was outdated (a newer file says otherwise), add the question to the bench yourself in the same session: one row in `~/.claude/scripts/recall-bench/questions.tsv` (set `miss`, the question as asked, the file holding the right answer, the right answer in one line), then run `CSET=miss bash ~/.claude/scripts/recall-bench/run.sh C` (~Update.06 a question) and note the result in that folder's `results.md`. Say so in one line. Eric will not remember to ask; the daily backup's recall check (`recall-bench/check.py`) then guards that question from then on.

## Daily compiled logs — read-only

`~/.claude/claude-memory-compiler/daily/{YYYY-MM-DD}.md` is produced by `claude-memory-compiler` through its own SessionEnd/PreCompact hooks, and injected by its own SessionStart hook.

- **Never hand-edit these files.** The compiler owns them.
- **Never read them eagerly.** Treat the injected snapshot as the source of truth.

## What is loaded at session start

`~/.claude/global-memory/USER.md` and `MEMORY.md` are read once at session start and are a **frozen snapshot**. Mid-session writes persist to disk but only take effect next session — this is deliberate, to preserve the prefix cache. Never load more than the startup set proactively.

## Rules

- Never exceed Tier B caps. Consolidate first.
- Always dedup before adding.
- For Tier A, the slug is the absolute cwd with every character other than a letter or digit replaced by `-` (Mac `~/DEV` → `-Users-kristinarash-DEV`, `~/.claude/skills` → `-Users-kristinarash--claude-skills`; the Mac keeps `_`: `~/DEV/CLI_Dev` → `-Users-kristinarash-DEV-CLI_Dev`; Windows `~/Desktop/DEV` → `C--Users-eric-rash-Desktop-DEV`; `00_Primary_Storage_Drive` → `00-Primary-Storage-Drive`). The harness injects the correct slug each session — use that, don't reconstruct it.
- **Write only to the current machine's slug.** Both machines are active as of 2026-09-10: Mac slugs are `-Users-kristinarash-*`, Windows slugs are `C--Users-eric-rash-*`. A fact written to the other machine's slug is never auto-injected here (memsearch still finds it). Durable project facts belong in the repo's `docs/` so both machines see them.
- Never announce the write mid-session beyond the one-line confirmation. The injected snapshot is frozen — the new fact appears next session, not this one.

## Verification Gate

After every write:

1. Read the exact destination back and require the intended fact to appear once in the intended tier.
2. Re-run the Tier B character cap check after the write.
3. Check the surrounding section for an unresolved contradiction or stale duplicate. Resolve it or report `FAIL`.
4. For Tier A, verify the new file has valid frontmatter and the memory index pointer resolves to it.
5. Distinguish persisted state from activation: the write can pass now, but next-session injection remains unverified until a later session observes it.

Report `PASS` only when persistence, uniqueness, tier placement, caps, and pointers are verified. Report `FAIL` with the target path and failed check otherwise. Do not emit “Saved” before read-back succeeds.

skills.name: workflow-authoring
skills.content:
# Workflow authoring reference

A workflow structures work across many agents — to be comprehensive (decompose and cover in parallel), to be confident (independent perspectives and adversarial checks before committing), or to take on scale one context can't hold (migrations, audits, broad sweeps). The script is where you encode that structure: what fans out, what verifies, what synthesizes.

When you do call it, the right move is often **hybrid**: scout inline first (list the files, find the channels, scope the diff) to discover the work-list, then call Workflow to pipeline over it. You don't need to know the shape before the *task* — only before the *orchestration step*.

Common single-phase workflows you can chain across turns:
- **Understand** — parallel readers over relevant subsystems → structured map
- **Design** — judge panel of N independent approaches → scored synthesis
- **Review** — dimensions → find → adversarially verify (the review-changes example)
- **Research** — multi-modal sweep → deep-read → synthesize
- **Migrate** — discover sites → transform each (worktree isolation) → verify

For larger work, run several in sequence — read each result before deciding the next phase. You stay in the loop; each workflow is one well-scoped fan-out.

**Ultracode.** When a system-reminder confirms ultracode is on, that opt-in is standing: author and run a workflow for every substantive task by default. The goal is the most exhaustive, correct answer you can produce — token cost is not a constraint. For multi-phase work (understand → design → implement → review), that often means several workflows in sequence — one per phase — so you stay in the loop between them. The quality patterns below (adversarial verify, multi-modal sweep, completeness critic, loop-until-dry) are the tools; pick what fits the task. Lean toward orchestrating with workflows and adversarially verifying your findings — unless the work is trivial or already verified. Solo only on conversational turns or trivial mechanical edits. When a reminder says ultracode is off, revert to the opt-in rule in the Workflow tool description.

Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first. Every invocation automatically persists its script to a file under the session directory and returns the path in the tool result. To iterate on a workflow, edit that file with Write/Edit and re-invoke Workflow with `{scriptPath: "<path>"}` instead of resending the full script.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'find-flaky-tests',
    description: 'Find flaky tests and propose fixes',   // one-line, shown in permission dialog
    phases: [                                            // one entry per phase() call
      { title: 'Scan', detail: 'grep test logs for retries' },
      { title: 'Fix', detail: 'one agent per flaky test' },
    ],
  }
  // script body starts here — use agent()/parallel()/pipeline()/phase()/log()
  phase('Scan')
  const flaky = await agent('grep CI logs for retry markers', {schema: FLAKY_SCHEMA})
  ...

The `meta` object must be a PURE LITERAL — no variables, function calls, spreads, or template interpolation. Required fields: `name`, `description`. Optional: `whenToUse` (shown in the workflow list), `phases`. Use the SAME phase titles in meta.phases as in phase() calls — titles are matched exactly; a phase() call with no matching meta entry just gets its own progress group. Add `model` to a phase entry when that phase uses a specific model override.

Script body hooks:
- agent(prompt: string, opts?: {label?: string, phase?: string, schema?: object, model?: string, effort?: string, isolation?: 'worktree', agentType?: string}): Promise<any> — spawn a subagent. Without schema, returns its final text as a string. With schema (a JSON Schema), the subagent is forced to call a StructuredOutput tool and agent() returns the validated object — no parsing needed. Returns null if the user skips the agent mid-run or the subagent dies on a terminal API error after retries (filter with .filter(Boolean)). opts.label overrides the display label. opts.phase explicitly assigns this agent to a progress group (use this inside pipeline()/parallel() stages to avoid races on the global phase() state — same phase string → same group box). opts.model overrides the model for this agent call. Default to omitting it — the agent inherits the main-loop model (the resolved session model), which is almost always correct. Only set it when you're highly confident a different tier fits the task; when unsure, omit. opts.effort overrides the reasoning effort for this agent call ('low' | 'medium' | 'high' | 'xhigh' | 'max') — omit to inherit the session effort; use 'low' for cheap mechanical stages and higher tiers only for the hardest verify/judge stages. opts.isolation: 'worktree' runs the agent in a fresh git worktree — EXPENSIVE (~200-500ms setup + disk per agent), use ONLY when agents mutate files in parallel and would otherwise conflict; the worktree is auto-removed if unchanged. opts.agentType uses a custom subagent type (e.g. 'general-purpose', 'code-reviewer') instead of the default workflow subagent — resolved from the same registry as the Agent tool; composes with schema (the custom agent's system prompt gets a StructuredOutput instruction appended).
- pipeline(items, stage1, stage2, ...): Promise<any[]> — run each item through all stages independently, NO barrier between stages. Item A can be in stage 3 while item B is still in stage 1. This is the DEFAULT for multi-stage work. Wall-clock = slowest single-item chain, not sum-of-slowest-per-stage. Every stage callback receives (prevResult, originalItem, index) — use originalItem/index in later stages to label work without threading context through stage 1's return value. A stage that throws drops that item to `null` and skips its remaining stages.
- parallel(thunks: Array<() => Promise<any>>): Promise<any[]> — run tasks concurrently. This is a BARRIER: awaits all thunks before returning. A thunk that throws (or whose agent errors) resolves to `null` in the result array — the call itself never rejects, so `.filter(Boolean)` before using the results. Use ONLY when you genuinely need all results together.
- log(message: string): void — emit a progress message to the user (shown as a narrator line above the progress tree)
- phase(title: string): void — start a new phase; subsequent agent() calls are grouped under this title in the progress display
- args: any — the value passed as Workflow's `args` input, verbatim (undefined if not provided). Pass arrays/objects as actual JSON values in the tool call, NOT as a JSON-encoded string — `args: ["a.ts", "b.ts"]`, not `args: "[\"a.ts\", ...]"` (a stringified list reaches the script as one string, so `args.filter`/`args.map` throw). Use this to parameterize named workflows — e.g. pass a research question, target path, or config object directly instead of via a side-channel file.
- budget: {total: number|null, spent(): number, remaining(): number} — the turn's token target from the user's "+500k"-style directive. `budget.total` is null if no target was set. `budget.spent()` returns output tokens spent this turn across the main loop and all workflows — the pool is shared, not per-workflow. `budget.remaining()` returns `max(0, total - spent())`, or `Infinity` if no target. The target is a HARD ceiling, not advisory: once `spent()` reaches `total`, further `agent()` calls throw. Use for dynamic loops: `while (budget.total && budget.remaining() > 50_000) { ... }`, or static scaling: `const FLEET = budget.total ? Math.floor(budget.total / 100_000) : 5`.
- workflow(nameOrRef: string | {scriptPath: string}, args?: any): Promise<any> — run another workflow inline as a sub-step and return whatever it returns. Pass a name to invoke a saved workflow (same registry as {name: "..."}), or {scriptPath} to run a script file you Wrote earlier. The child shares this run's concurrency cap, agent counter, abort signal, and token budget — its agents appear under a "▸ name" group in /workflows and its tokens count toward budget.spent(). The args param becomes the child's `args` global. Nesting is one level only: workflow() inside a child throws. Throws on unknown name / unreadable scriptPath / child syntax error; catch to handle gracefully.

Subagents are told their final text IS the return value (not a human-facing message), so they return raw data. For structured output, use the schema option — validation happens at the tool-call layer so the model retries on mismatch.
Schemas need {type: 'object', properties: {...}} at root and required ⊆ properties; unsatisfiable ones throw at agent().

Workflow agents can reach all session-connected MCP tools via ToolSearch — schemas load on demand per agent. Caveat: interactively-authenticated MCP servers (e.g. claude.ai) may be absent in headless/cron runs.

Subagents get the same CLAUDE.md files injected at start that you did (except built-in agent types that omit them, such as Explore and Plan) — don't tell them to re-read those or paste their rules into the prompt; name the specific rule a stage needs, if any.

Scripts are plain JavaScript, NOT TypeScript — type annotations (`: string[]`), interfaces, and generics fail to parse. The script body runs in an async context — use await directly. Standard JS built-ins (JSON, Math, Array, etc.) are available — EXCEPT `Date.now()`/`Math.random()`/argless `new Date()`, which throw (they would break resume); pass timestamps in via `args`, stamp results after the workflow returns, and for randomness vary the agent prompt/label by index. No filesystem or Node.js API access.

DEFAULT TO pipeline(). Only reach for a barrier (parallel between stages) when you genuinely need ALL prior-stage results together.

A barrier is correct ONLY when stage N needs cross-item context from all of stage N-1:
- Dedup/merge across the full result set before expensive downstream work
- Early-exit if the total count is zero ("0 bugs found → skip verification entirely")
- Stage N's prompt references "the other findings" for comparison

A barrier is NOT justified by:
- "I need to flatten/map/filter first" — do it inside a pipeline stage: pipeline(items, stageA, r => transform([r]).flat(), stageB)
- "The stages are conceptually separate" — that's what pipeline() models. Separate stages ≠ synchronized stages.
- "It's cleaner code" — barrier latency is real. If 5 finders run and the slowest takes 3× the fastest, a barrier wastes 2/3 of the fast finders' idle time.

Smell test: if you wrote
  const a = await parallel(...)
  const b = transform(a)        // flatten, map, filter — no cross-item dependency
  const c = await parallel(b.map(...))
that middle transform doesn't need the barrier. Rewrite as a pipeline with the transform inside a stage. When in doubt: pipeline.

Concurrent agent() calls are capped at min(16, available CPUs - 2) per workflow — excess calls queue and run as slots free up. You can still pass 100 items to parallel()/pipeline() and they all complete; only ~10 run at any moment. Total agent count across a workflow's lifetime is capped at 1000 — a runaway-loop backstop set far above any real workflow. A single parallel()/pipeline() call accepts at most 4096 items; passing more is an explicit error, not a silent truncation.

When a barrier IS correct — dedup across all findings before expensive verification:
  const all = await parallel(DIMENSIONS.map(d => () => agent(d.prompt, {schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA})))
  const deduped = dedupeByFileAndLine(all.filter(Boolean).flatMap(r => r.findings))  // <-- genuinely needs ALL at once
  const verified = await parallel(deduped.map(f => () => agent(verifyPrompt(f), {schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})))

Loop-until-count pattern — accumulate to a target:
  const bugs = []
  while (bugs.length < 10) {
    const result = await agent("Find bugs in this codebase.", {schema: BUGS_SCHEMA})
    bugs.push(...result.bugs)
    log(`${bugs.length}/10 found`)
  }

Loop-until-budget pattern — scale depth to the user's "+500k" directive. Guard on budget.total: with no target set, remaining() is Infinity and the loop would run straight to the 1000-agent cap.
  const bugs = []
  while (budget.total && budget.remaining() > 50_000) {
    const result = await agent("Find bugs in this codebase.", {schema: BUGS_SCHEMA})
    bugs.push(...result.bugs)
    log(`${bugs.length} found, ${Math.round(budget.remaining()/1000)}k remaining`)
  }

Composing patterns — exhaustive review (find → dedup vs seen → diverse-lens panel → loop-until-dry):
  const seen = new Set(), confirmed = []
  let dry = 0
  while (dry < 2) {                                              // loop-until-dry
    const found = (await parallel(FINDERS.map(f => () =>          // barrier: collect all finders this round
      agent(f.prompt, {phase: 'Find', schema: BUGS})))).filter(Boolean).flatMap(r => r.bugs)
    const fresh = found.filter(b => !seen.has(key(b)))           // dedup vs ALL seen — plain code, not an agent
    if (!fresh.length) { dry++; continue }
    dry = 0; fresh.forEach(b => seen.add(key(b)))
    const judged = await parallel(fresh.map(b => () =>           // every fresh bug judged concurrently...
      parallel(['correctness','security','repro'].map(lens => () =>   // ...each by 3 distinct lenses
        agent(`Judge "${b.desc}" via the ${lens} lens — real?`, {phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT})))
        .then(vs => ({ b, real: vs.filter(Boolean).filter(v => v.real).length >= 2 }))))
    confirmed.push(...judged.filter(v => v.real).map(v => v.b))
  }
  return confirmed
  // dedup vs `seen`, NOT `confirmed` — else judge-rejected findings reappear every round and it never converges.

Quality patterns — common shapes; pick by task and compose freely:
- Adversarial verify: spawn N independent skeptics per finding, each prompted to REFUTE. Kill if ≥majority refute. Prevents plausible-but-wrong findings from surviving.
    const votes = await parallel(Array.from({length: 3}, () => () =>
      agent(`Try to refute: ${claim}. Default to refuted=true if uncertain.`, {schema: VERDICT})))
    const survives = votes.filter(Boolean).filter(v => !v.refuted).length >= 2
- Perspective-diverse verify: when a finding can fail in more than one way, give each verifier a distinct lens (correctness, security, perf, does-it-reproduce) instead of N identical refuters — diversity catches failure modes redundancy can't.
- Judge panel: generate N independent attempts from different angles (e.g. MVP-first, risk-first, user-first), score with parallel judges, synthesize from the winner while grafting the best ideas from runners-up. Beats one-attempt-iterated when the solution space is wide.
- Loop-until-dry: for unknown-size discovery (bugs, issues, edge cases), keep spawning finders until K consecutive rounds return nothing new. Simple counters (while count < N) miss the tail.
- Multi-modal sweep: parallel agents each searching a different way (by-container, by-content, by-entity, by-time). Each is blind to what the others surface; useful when one search angle won't find everything.
- Completeness critic: a final agent that asks "what's missing — modality not run, claim unverified, source unread?" What it finds becomes the next round of work.
- No silent caps: if a workflow bounds coverage (top-N, no-retry, sampling), `log()` what was dropped — silent truncation reads as "covered everything" when it didn't.

Scale to what the user asked for. "find any bugs" → a few finders, single-vote verify. "thoroughly audit this" or "be comprehensive" → larger finder pool, 3–5 vote adversarial pass, synthesis stage. When unsure, lean toward thoroughness for research/review/audit requests and toward brevity for quick checks.

These patterns aren't exhaustive — compose novel harnesses when the task calls for it (tournament brackets, self-repair loops, staged escalation, whatever fits).

Use this tool for multi-step orchestration where control flow should be deterministic (loops, conditionals, fan-out) rather than model-driven.

## Resume

The tool result includes a runId. To resume after a pause, kill, or script edit, relaunch with Workflow({scriptPath, resumeFromRunId}) — the longest unchanged prefix of agent() calls returns cached results instantly; the first edited/new call and everything after it runs live. Same script + same args → 100% cache hit. Before diagnosing why a completed workflow returned an empty or unexpected result, Read <transcriptDir>/journal.jsonl — it records each agent's actual return value; do not assume cached results are non-empty. Date.now()/Math.random()/new Date() are unavailable in scripts (they would break this) — stamp results after the workflow returns, or pass timestamps via args. Fallback when no journal is available: Read agent-<id>.jsonl files in the transcript directory and hand-author a continuation script.

### Skill: memory-write
Path: userSettings:memory-write

Base directory for this skill: /Users/kristinarash/.claude/skills/memory-write

# Memory Write

## Outcome
- Fact added to, updated in, or removed from the correct memory tier
- Tier-B caps enforced (2,500 chars for MEMORY.md, 1,375 for USER.md)
- Confirmation: "Saved — will be active from next session."

## Pick the tier first

Ask: "Will this fact still be true and useful in 3 months, across multiple projects?"

**Tier A — `~/.claude/projects/<slug>/memory/`** (one file per fact, indexed by MEMORY.md)
- Durable user facts → `user_*.md` (metadata.type: user)
- Stable project conventions / gotchas → `project_*.md` (metadata.type: project)
- Behavioral feedback rules → `feedback_*.md` (metadata.type: feedback)
- External-system pointers → `reference_*.md` (metadata.type: reference)

**Tier B — `~/.claude/global-memory/`** (single capped file)
- Active threads (in-progress work) → `MEMORY.md` `## Active Threads`
- Current env notes (URLs, tool versions, project structure in play) → `MEMORY.md` `## Environment Notes`
- Pending decisions → `MEMORY.md` `## Pending Decisions`
- Durable user profile updates → `USER.md`

## Steps

1. **Decide tier** using the rule above.
2. **Read** the target file in full.
3. **Dedup check** — substring scan; if the fact already exists, skip or update in place.
4. **Cap check** for Tier B — `wc -c < ~/.claude/global-memory/MEMORY.md` (or USER.md). If over cap, consolidate (merge similar entries, prune stale) before adding.
5. **Write** the change.
   - Tier A: create a new file with proper frontmatter (name, description, metadata.type) and add a one-line pointer to that slug's `MEMORY.md` index. `name:` follows the rule below. Do it in one call, from the project folder (the slug comes from the current folder; `--dir` overrides):
     `python3 ~/.claude/scripts/remember.py --type <t> --name <bare-slug> --desc "<one line>" --hook "<when to open>" [--why "..." --how "..."] "<fact>"`
     It checks the name rule, refuses an existing or look-alike name (exit 2: read that file, then `--update` it or `--force`), writes the file and the index line, runs steps 1 and 4 of the Verification Gate, and refreshes recall.py's index. `PASS` covers those checks; step 3 (contradictions) is still yours.
   - Tier B: append under the correct `##` section.
6. **Confirm** in one line: `Saved — will be active from next session.`

## The `name:` field — bare kebab slug

**`name:` = the filename stem minus its leading type token, kebab-cased.** The type
already lives in `metadata.type` and the filename already carries the prefix; repeating
it in `name:` is the third copy.

| File | `name:` |
|---|---|
| `project_automation-cadence.md` | `automation-cadence` |
| `user_sports-teams.md` | `sports-teams` |
| `reference_baylor-house-style.md` | `baylor-house-style` |
| `feedback_project_idea_capture.md` | `project-idea-capture` |

Note the last row: strip only the **leading** token. `feedback_project_idea_capture.md`
is a feedback memory *about* project-idea capture — its name keeps the word `project`.

`[[links]]` target this bare name, never the filename and never a prefixed variant.

This rule exists because it was previously unwritten: an audit on 2026-09-02 found the
corpus split 59 bare / 58 prefixed, which broke 37 links. Both forms look right in
isolation, so without a stated rule the split regrows on every write.

## Actions

- **add** — append (default)
- **replace** — substring match + swap. Preferred over add when updating an existing fact.
- **remove** — confirm with the user before deleting.

## Retrieval — the tiered ladder

When the user asks about past context, decisions, or "did we already…?", climb in order and stop as soon as the question is answered. Do not run a search when the answer is already in the injected snapshot.

1. **Tier 0** — scan what is already in context (USER.md, MEMORY.md, today's compiled log). Zero cost.
2. **L1** — `python3 ~/.claude/scripts/recall.py "question"`. Plain code, ~1 s: BM25 keyword rank over the memsearch paths plus the whole vault, a Tier A memory first, then it opens the best file and prints the matching paragraphs with line numbers. Answer from that. If the printed paragraphs miss the answer, open the #2 or #3 candidate it lists.
3. **L2** — on `NO MATCH`, or when the words in the question are not the words in the notes: `memsearch search "query" --top-k 5`. Hybrid vector + keyword, ~1 min: Tier A files (including the Windows-machine slugs), daily logs, transcripts.
4. **L3** — `memsearch expand <chunk_hash>`. Full markdown section around a hit.
5. **L4** — `memsearch transcript <session_id>`. Raw dialogue. Last resort.
6. **Fallback** — say "I don't have a record of that."

**A recall that turned out wrong or stale becomes a test question — without being asked.** When Eric corrects a recalled fact, or you find that the answer you gave from recall was outdated (a newer file says otherwise), add the question to the bench yourself in the same session: one row in `~/.claude/scripts/recall-bench/questions.tsv` (set `miss`, the question as asked, the file holding the right answer, the right answer in one line), then run `CSET=miss bash ~/.claude/scripts/recall-bench/run.sh C` (~Update.06 a question) and note the result in that folder's `results.md`. Say so in one line. Eric will not remember to ask; the daily backup's recall check (`recall-bench/check.py`) then guards that question from then on.

## Daily compiled logs — read-only

`~/.claude/claude-memory-compiler/daily/{YYYY-MM-DD}.md` is produced by `claude-memory-compiler` through its own SessionEnd/PreCompact hooks, and injected by its own SessionStart hook.

- **Never hand-edit these files.** The compiler owns them.
- **Never read them eagerly.** Treat the injected snapshot as the source of truth.

## What is loaded at session start

`~/.claude/global-memory/USER.md` and `MEMORY.md` are read once at session start and are a **frozen snapshot**. Mid-session writes persist to disk but only take effect next session — this is deliberate, to preserve the prefix cache. Never load more than the startup set proactively.

## Rules

- Never exceed Tier B caps. Consolidate first.
- Always dedup before adding.
- For Tier A, the slug is the absolute cwd with every character other than a letter or digit replaced by `-` (Mac `~/DEV` → `-Users-kristinarash-DEV`, `~/.claude/skills` → `-Users-kristinarash--claude-skills`; the Mac keeps `_`: `~/DEV/CLI_Dev` → `-Users-kristinarash-DEV-CLI_Dev`; Windows `~/Desktop/DEV` → `C--Users-eric-rash-Desktop-DEV`; `00_Primary_Storage_Drive` → `00-Primary-Storage-Drive`). The harness injects the correct slug each session — use that, don't reconstruct it.
- **Write only to the current machine's slug.** Both machines are active as of 2026-09-10: Mac slugs are `-Users-kristinarash-*`, Windows slugs are `C--Users-eric-rash-*`. A fact written to the other machine's slug is never auto-injected here (memsearch still finds it). Durable project facts belong in the repo's `docs/` so both machines see them.
- Never announce the write mid-session beyond the one-line confirmation. The injected snapshot is frozen — the new fact appears next session, not this one.

## Verification Gate

After every write:

1. Read the exact destination back and require the intended fact to appear once in the intended tier.
2. Re-run the Tier B character cap check after the write.
3. Check the surrounding section for an unresolved contradiction or stale duplicate. Resolve it or report `FAIL`.
4. For Tier A, verify the new file has valid frontmatter and the memory index pointer resolves to it.
5. Distinguish persisted state from activation: the write can pass now, but next-session injection remains unverified until a later session observes it.

Report `PASS` only when persistence, uniqueness, tier placement, caps, and pointers are verified. Report `FAIL` with the target path and failed check otherwise. Do not emit “Saved” before read-back succeeds.
